q: Dry ice is the solid form of what substance?
e: Dry ice is really frozen carbon dioxide gas, skipping the messy puddle stage to vanish right back into chilly air!

q: Which element has the highest melting point?
e: Carbon hugs its tiny atoms so tightly that it can survive inside blazing heat where every other element melts away.

q: Naturally occuring uranium primarily consists of which isotope?
e: Uranium-238 is the heavyweight champ that makes up over ninety-nine percent of all the natural uranium resting in the ground.

q: What is the atomic mass of Carbon?
e: Carbon balances six protons and six neutrons inside its tiny heart, giving this busy life-builder an atomic mass of twelve.

q: Which element has the chemical symbol 'Fe'?
e: Iron borrowed its Fe name tag from ferrum, an old Latin word for this tough, trusty metal.

q: The element involved in making human blood red is which of the following?
e: Iron catches fresh oxygen in your blood and blushes bright red, painting every heartbeat with vibrant color!

q: Which gas forms about 78% of the Earth’s atmosphere?
e: Nitrogen quietly fills most of our sky, wrapping the whole world in a giant, invisible blanket.

q: What is the first element on the periodic table?
e: Light and cheerful hydrogen has just one proton, proudly leading the giant parade of elements at spot number one.

q: Salt is 100% composed of Sodium.
e: That is false because table salt is a tasty friendship between sodium and chlorine, working as a team.

q: Which of the following is not one of the groups on the periodic table?
e: Fluorine is just one feisty element in the halogen family, so Fluorines is not a real group name.

q: What is the chemical symbol for Helium?
e: Helium simply borrows the first two letters of its cheerful name to get its symbol, He.

q: Water always boils at 100°C, 212°F, 373.15K, no matter where you are.
e: This is false because high up on chilly mountains, lighter air lets water bubble and boil at lower temperatures.

q: Which of these Elements is a metalloid?
e: Antimony is a metalloid because it acts like a magical mix, shining like metal but crumbling like rock.

q: Who is the chemical element Curium named after?
e: Curium honors Marie and Pierre Curie, two brilliant partners who spent their lives unlocking the secrets of radioactivity.

q: What is the common name of the chemical compound "dihydrogen monoxide"?
e: Dihydrogen monoxide is just a fancy science name for water, meaning two hydrogens hugging one oxygen!

q: An exothermic reaction is a chemical reaction that releases energy by radiating electricity.
e: This is false because exothermic reactions prefer to give off cozy heat and light, not sparks of electricity.

q: Which noble gas has the lowest atomic number?
e: Helium floats at the very top of the noble gas family, proudly carrying an atomic number of just two.

q: Which is the most abundant element in the universe?
e: Hydrogen was the universe's first creation, and it still fills nearly three-quarters of all space with starlight!

q: What is the chemical makeup of water?
e: Water is H2O because two eager hydrogen atoms team up with one oxygen atom to make every splashing drop.

q: Stars consist mainly of hydrogen and which other gas?
e: Stars cook hydrogen into heaps of helium, fueling their warm, fiery glow across the deep dark night.

q: This element, when overcome with extreme heat and pressure, creates diamonds.
e: Deep underground, humble carbon atoms squeeze together in a giant warm hug until they sparkle into brilliant diamonds.

q: What is the elemental symbol for mercury?
e: Mercury borrows its symbol Hg from an ancient name meaning silver water, dancing around like shiny liquid metal.

q: Au on the Periodic Table refers to which element?
e: Au stands for gold, coming from an old word for glowing dawn, shining bright like buried treasure.

q: Which element has the atomic number of 7?
e: Nitrogen proudly carries seven protons in its heart, floating all around us to fill up the big blue sky.

q: In the periodic table, Potassium's symbol is the letter K.
e: It is true, because potassium borrows the letter K from its historic name, kalium, to keep things fun.

q: What is the atomic number of Uranium
e: Uranium proudly packs ninety-two positive protons right at its bustling heart.

q: What polymer is used to make CDs, safety goggles and riot shields?
e: Polycarbonate is tough yet crystal clear, making it perfect for shields that take hard hits without breaking!

q: Which one of these scientists conducted the Gold Foil Experiment which concluded that atoms are mostly made of empty space?
e: Ernest Rutherford shot tiny beams at golden foil and gasped to discover that atoms are mostly empty, open space.

q: Deionized water is water with which of the following removed?
e: Deionizing sweeps away charged mineral visitors like iron, leaving the water delightfully pure and free of stray electric charges.

q: Which of the following men does not have a chemical element named after him?
e: Even though an apple helped him discover gravity, Sir Isaac Newton never got his own element on the periodic table.

q: The Sun consists of mostly which two elements?
e: Our glowing Sun is a giant, crackling campfire built almost entirely from swirling hydrogen and helium.

q: Which of these elements on the Periodic Table is a Noble Gas?
e: Neon is a calm noble gas that glows happily in signs and keeps its electrons all to itself.

q: What is the chemical formula for ammonia?
e: One friendly nitrogen atom holds hands with three loyal hydrogens, creating the smelly little recipe we call NH3.

q: After which Danish city is the 72th element on the periodic table named?
e: Hafnium was discovered in lovely Copenhagen, taking its name from the ancient, storybook word for that very city.

q: Along with Oxygen, which element is primarily responsible for the sky appearing blue?
e: Nitrogen fills most of our air, happily scattering blue sunlight in every direction to paint the sky above us.

q: Steel is an alloy of Iron and Carbon.
e: It is true because strong iron mixes with a pinch of carbon to become super-tough steel!

q: What is the atomic number of the element Strontium?
e: Deep inside every strontium atom, thirty-eight cheerful protons keep its cozy center glowing bright with personality.

q: Deuterium is an isotope of which element?
e: Deuterium is simply a hydrogen atom that packed an extra neutron friend into its backpack, making it a bit heavier!

q: A positron is an antiparticle of a what?
e: A positron is the mirror twin of an electron, matching its tiny size perfectly but wearing a positive charge instead.

q: What is the chemical symbol for lead?
e: Heavy lead wears the symbol Pb because ancient Romans called it plumbum when making water pipes.

q: On the periodic table of elements, what is the symbol for Tin?
e: Tin borrows its symbol Sn from its ancient Latin name, stannum, like a secret code from the past!

q: In Chemistry, how many isomers does Butanol (C4H9OH) have?
e: Butanol's atoms can hold hands in four uniquely shaped ways, giving it four cool isomers!

q: Which chemical element has the lowest boiling point?
e: Helium atoms are super independent and barely stick together, boiling into gas at the coldest temperature around.

q: Which chemical element was originally known as Alabamine?
e: Before getting named astatine, element 85 was called alabamine by researchers who thought they found it in Alabama.

q: During beta decay, carbon-14 decays into nitrogen-14 along with an electron and what other particle?
e: When the electron zooms away, a tiny, ghost-like antineutrino zips out alongside it to balance the cosmic books.

q: At 100 degrees Fahrenheit, which of the following substances would feel hottest to touch?
e: Gold is such a speedy heat conductor that it rushes its warmth into your fingers way faster than the others.

q: Which of the following elements possesses the highest ionization energy?
e: Neon is a noble gas with a full, happy family of electrons, so it clutches them tightly and stubbornly refuses to let any go.

q: A balanced chemical equation must possess which of the following?
a: The same number of molecules on both sides of the equation
The same kinds of molecules on both sides of the equation
The same number of each kind of atom on both sides of the equation
The same leading coefficient on both sides of the equation
e: Atoms love fair play, so a balanced equation keeps the exact same number of each atom on both sides.

q: For a brick of gold, which of the following properties would change if you transported the brick from the surface of the Earth to the surface of the Moon?
e: The brick keeps all its stuff, but the Moon pulls more gently, so its weight drops magically!

q: Which of the following defines a pure substance that cannot be broken down by any chemical means?
e: An element is nature's purest building block, so wonderfully simple that no chemical reaction can break it down any further.

q: Which of the following processes is exothermic:
a: solid water changes to water vapor
solid water changes to liquid water
liquid water changes to solid water
liquid water changes to water vapor
e: As wiggly liquid water cuddles together to freeze into solid ice, it releases warmth into the air, making it exothermic!

q: Although this is dangerous, if you hypothetically were to breathe in xenon or krypton instead of helium, what would happen to the sound of your voice?
a: It would be lower than when you breathe helium and also lower than your regular voice
It would be lower than when you breathe helium, but higher than your regular voice
It would be the same as when you breathe helium
It would be higher than when you breathe helium
e: Heavy xenon gas slows sound waves down like molasses, turning your voice into a deep, rumbling giant’s growl.

q: With which of the following is Brownian motion most directly related:
e: Thermal energy is pure heat, which makes invisible water molecules dance and bump floating specks all around the room.

q: Heating an endothermic reaction will shift equilibrium towards which of the following?
e: Endothermic reactions love warmth, so feeding them heat happily pushes everything forward to make more products!

q: Which of the following scientific principles is based on the conservation of electric charge?
e: Every electric charge marching into a crossroad must march back out, because charges can never just vanish into thin air.

q: When a substance contains more of a dissolved compound than can be dissolved by the solvent under standard conditions, it is referred to as which of the following?
e: When a drink is tricked into holding even more sweetness than it normally can, it becomes super saturated!

q: Which of the following quantities is dimensionless?
a: The volume of an internal combustion engine
The number of molecules in 1 gram of water
The mass of one mole of sodium atoms
e: Counting molecules is just tallying up tiny friends, so it gives a pure number with no units like meters or grams attached.

q: Which of the following is NOT a salt:
e: Potassium hydroxide carries a slippery hydroxide piece that makes it a powerful base instead of a true salt!

q: Which of the following is a characteristic of all strong acids?
e: The moment strong acids dive into water, all their tiny parts joyfully let go and split completely apart.

q: Methoxyethane is an example of what class of organic molecule?
e: An oxygen atom happily holds hands between two carbon groups, making methoxyethane a classic member of the ether family.

q: Lighter gases diffuse more quickly than heavier gases. Mathematically, this is expressed by which of the following laws?
e: Graham's law discovered that lightweight gas puffballs can sprint and spread through a room much faster than bulky, heavy ones.

q: Distillation will NOT work very well under which of the following situations:
a: the components in the mixture have the same boiling points
the mixture consists of a solid and a liquid
e: Distillation separates liquids by boiling them apart, but if they boil at the exact same temperature, they fly away together like best friends!

q: Biopolymers are, in general, what type of polymer?
e: Nature snaps living chains together by squeezing out tiny drops of water, making biopolymers clever condensation polymers.

q: The cesium atom is used to define which of the following SI units?
e: Cesium atoms tick-tock with super steady vibrations, making them the ultimate tiny clock used to define the second.

q: Silver nitrate reacts with copper metal to form copper nitrate and silver metal. What type of reaction is this?
e: Copper tosses tiny electrons over to silver like a friendly game of catch, making this a redox swap!

q: Which of the following elements has the lowest atomic number?
e: With sixty-six protons in its center, dysprosium has fewer than the others, giving it the lowest atomic number on this list.

q: Which of the following compounds is covalently bonded?
e: In carbon monoxide, carbon and oxygen act like friendly neighbors who share their electrons instead of giving them away.

q: When plotting the energy of the components of a slow reaction, such as the conversion of diamond into graphite, versus the reaction progress, which of the following best represents the shape of the curve?
e: Atoms must climb an energetic little mountain called activation energy before rolling downhill, making a peak in the middle.

q: Which of the following statements is LEAST accurate regarding states of matter:
a: gases can be made of a single element
matter on Earth is never in a plasma state
e: Lightning bolts sizzle with fiery plasma right here on Earth, so plasma is definitely not missing from our world!

q: The particles of which of the following states of matter have the strongest attraction between them?
e: Particles in a solid hug each other super tightly, refusing to let go because their attraction is the strongest around!

q: When water is electrolyzed, what collects at the anode?
e: Electricity splits water apart, sending cheerful oxygen bubbles straight up to the positive anode to greet the world.

q: The behavior of light has lead scientists to generally consider light as behaving as:
e: Light loves playing dress-up! Sometimes it zips along like tiny bouncing balls, and other times it ripples like gentle ocean waves.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about phase changes in substances:
a: energy is exchanged during a phase change
sublimation is a type of phase change involving solids
freezing is an exothermic phase change
a phase change cannot be reversed
e: Phase changes love to backtrack, so melted ice can always freeze right back into a solid cube!

q: Which of the following pairs of elements are liquid at room temperature?
e: Mercury and bromine are the only two special elements that stay runny like puddle water at ordinary room temperature.

q: Which of the following four processes is endothermic?
e: An ice cube melts by drinking in warmth from the air, making it an endothermic heat-sponge.

q: Which of the following elements does not occur naturally in nature:
e: Technetium is a shy element that nature forgot to make, so curious scientists had to create it in a lab!

q: Alkali metals like sodium give up electrons when forming ionic bonds. In these ionic compounds, what is their typical oxidation number?
e: Giving away one negative electron leaves these friendly metals with a tidy positive 1 charge.

q: Which of the following statements is TRUE of buffers:
a: all neutral pH solutions have equal numbers of buffers
hydronium ions are present in large amounts in most buffers
certain buffers will absorb hydrogen ions to prevent a change in a solution's pH
buffers are artificial chemicals rarely found in nature
e: Helpful buffers act like little sponges, soaking up stray hydrogen ions so the liquid stays peaceful and keeps its balance.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of the Earth's magnetic field?
a: It is created by the molten iron in the Earth's outer core
The intensity of the field is the same at the poles and at the equator
It is possible that in a few hundred thousand years, the Earth's magnetic north pole will be reversed
e: Earth's magnetic blanket pulls much tighter at the icy poles than at the equator, so its strength is never identical everywhere.

q: Which of the following is an example of a compound with an ionic bond?
e: Sodium happily gives electrons away to sulfur like a gift, creating charged partners that stick together with an ionic bond!

q: What state of matter has a definite volume but not a definite shape?
e: A liquid happily takes the shape of whatever cup it visits, but it always keeps the exact same amount of splash!

q: Which of the following actions would NOT change the strength of an air core electromagnet?
a: Inserting an iron core inside the loop
e: Turning the electric flow backwards only flips the magnet's poles upside down without weakening its mighty pulling power.

q: A litmus paper test is used to determine:
a: whether a solution is acidic or basic
e: Litmus paper cleverly shifts color like a chameleon to reveal if a splash is sour acid or slippery base.

q: What is the primary component of natural gas?
e: Deep underground, natural gas is mostly made of friendly methane, a tiny fuel floating ready to create cozy warmth.

q: Which of the following is true of periodic trends?
a: The smaller the atom, the greater the ionization energy
The larger the electronegativity, the smaller the ionization energy
Elements with the highest metallic character are located at the upper left corner of the periodic table
The process of removing an electron from an atom is always exothermic
e: Tiny atoms hug their outer electrons super close, making it take tons of energy to yank one away!

q: Which of the following increases with the addition of sodium chloride to water?
a: The boiling point of the solution
The freezing point of the solution
The vapor pressure of the solution
e: Salt holds onto water molecules tightly, so they need a lot more heat before they can bubble and boil.

q: J. J. Thomson primarily used what instrument to discover electrons:
e: Thomson zapped glowing beams through a glass cathode ray tube to discover tiny zooming electrons!

q: Which of the following compounds is NOT used as fuel in a nuclear reactor?
e: Uranium-236 is the sleepy leftover made after splitting atoms, so it cannot be used as reactor fuel.

q: Which of the following characteristics best describes metals?
a: Brittle, highly reactive, and have low melting points
Lustrous, malleable, and are good conductors
Dense, form salts, and are highly reactive
Hard, form negatively charged ions, and are good resistors
e: True metals love to gleam in the light, bend gently instead of snapping, and pass electricity along like a baton.

q: Kate sips some juice and notices that it is sour. What can she reasonably hypothesize about the juice?
a: It would likely neutralize with acetic acid
It would likely neutralize with muriatic acid
e: Acids love to tickle our tongues with a sharp, tangy zip, which gives sour juices their puckery punch.

q: A saturated aqueous solution of potassium chloride contains 34 grams of solute. Which of the following terms best describes an aqueous solution containing 30 grams of potassium chloride?
e: Because the water could hold four more grams of salt snacks, it is still unsaturated and ready for more.

q: Which of the following elements can form a monatomic gas at standard temperature and pressure?
e: Neon is a noble loner with full electron shells, happily floating around all by itself as a single atom.

q: Which of the following is an accurate description of the liquid phase of matter?
e: Liquids love playing dress-up by changing shape to fit any cup, but they always keep the exact same volume.

q: Which of the following BEST describes the following reaction: 4Fe + 3O2 2Fe2O3
e: Iron and oxygen join hands to build shiny new rust, teaming up in a reaction called synthesis.

q: Which of the following metals is the least magnetic?
e: While cobalt, iron, and nickel love clinging to magnets, quiet titanium barely feels any magnetic pull at all.

q: In commercial bronze, which of the following terms best describes the copper?
e: Since bronze is mostly copper hosting a little bit of tin, copper acts as the welcoming solvent.

q: Which of the following has the most inertia:
e: Inertia is just how stubborn an object is against moving, and four kilograms of iron has the most mass to shove.

q: Which of the following reactions always releases heat?
e: Exothermic reactions love sharing their cozy energy, happily sending heat out into the world like a crackling campfire.

q: Which of the following is not part of Dalton's atomic theory?
a: All matter is composed of atoms of elements
Chemical reactions occur when atoms are rearranged
Atoms are composed of protons, neutrons and electrons
Atoms cannot be created or destroyed
e: Dalton imagined atoms as solid little marbles, long before scientists peeked inside and discovered protons, neutrons, and electrons playing within!

q: Which of the following BEST describes electrostatic induction?
a: It is caused by the influence of nearby charged objects
It occurs between two charged objects
It transfers electrons from a charged object to a neutral object
It produces voltage across a conductor by means of a magnetic field
e: Without even touching, a charged object can nudge charges inside a neighbor just by hovering nearby, which is electrostatic induction at work.

q: Your friend rubs a balloon on your head and your hair sticks to the balloon due to static electricity. This occurs because which of the following particles has been exchanged between your hair and the balloon?
e: Tiny, restless electrons leap from your hair onto the balloon, leaving your strands reaching up for a high five!

q: Atoms of the most active nonmetals have which of the following characteristics?
a: Small atomic radii and high ionization energies
Small atomic radii and low ionization energies
Large atomic radii and high ionization energies
Large atomic radii and low ionization energies
e: These tiny, energetic atoms hug their electrons tight and refuse to let go, staying small while pulling neighbors close!

q: What is the term for the heat content of a system?
e: Enthalpy is the special scientific name for all the cozy heat energy tucked inside a system's pockets.

q: Which of the following is the BEST example of a chemical reaction:
a: an acid is added to a clear solution in a test tube and a white substance appears and falls to the bottom of the test tube
milk is added to water and the water turns a milky color
e: When two clear liquids suddenly create a brand-new solid snow falling down, a true chemical change has occurred!

q: Which of the following best describes static electricity?
a: Any interaction between a person and a metal object
The charging of a neutral object by an electrically charged object
The net accumulation of electric charges on an object
The movement of electrons through a conducting material
e: It happens when a bunch of tiny electric charges pile up in one spot, just waiting to give you a tickly zap!

q: Which of the following pairs are allotropes?
e: Diamond and graphite are pure carbon cousins, built from the exact same atoms wearing two completely different, dazzling outfits.

q: At a particular temperature T and pressure P, carbon dioxide is in the vapor phase. Which of the following is NOT possible if the pressure of the vapor is increased while the temperature stays the same?
a: The vapor enters the compressible liquid phase
The vapor enters the solid phase without entering the liquid phase first
The vapor enters the solid phase and then enters the liquid phase
e: Squeezing carbon dioxide packs its particles closer, so a solid cannot magically melt into a looser liquid just from more squeezing.

q: Metallic bonding accounts for all but which of the following physical characteristics of metals:
e: Metals are wonderful at sharing heat, so they actually have fantastic thermal conductivity, not poor at all!

q: The pH scale can be used to quantify which of the following properties of a solution?
e: The colorful pH scale acts like a mood ring for liquids, measuring how sour an acid is or how high its basicity climbs.

q: Which of the following requires the most energy:
a: Raising the temperature of one gram of water by one degree Celsius
Changing one gram of ice from a solid to a liquid
Changing one gram of water from a liquid to a gas
Lowering the temperature of one gram of water by one degree Celsius
e: Water droplets love clinging together, so breaking them apart from liquid into floating gas takes the most energy.

q: Carbon-14 emits beta radiation and decays with a half life of 5730 years. Four half lives are about how long in years?
e: Multiplying one giant waiting period of 5,730 years by four gives a grand total of 22,920 years!

q: Which of the following is typically TRUE:
a: rare earth metals are also known as alkali metals
noble gases are very reactive elements
a reaction in equilibrium cannot move forward or backward
e: Combustion is just fire happily burning fuel, which always shares cozy heat with the world around it.

q: Which of the following chemical formulas gives an indication of the arrangement of atoms and bonds in a chemical compound:
e: A structural formula draws a little map, showing exactly how each atom connects and holds hands with its neighbors.

q: In which of the following processes does the entropy of the system decrease?
e: When silver chloride precipitates, messy floating particles snap together into neat solid crystals, tidying up the room.

q: Which of the following properties is NOT a property of a covalent molecular compound?
e: Covalent molecules keep their electrons tightly tucked away, meaning electricity cannot zip through them easily.

q: Which of the following most closely relates to the first law of thermodynamics:
a: energy moving from a cold to a hot object
kinetic energy of molecules and atoms
e: Energy is a master shapeshifter that never truly disappears, only trading one costume for another because energy is always conserved.

q: Which of the following would be the most logical choice for neutralizing a small amount of basic sodium hydroxide that was spilled on a lab bench:
e: Gentle citric acid calms down the harsh spill safely, like squeezing friendly lemon juice instead of splashing fiery acids.

q: Which of the following elements is a metalloid?
e: Silicon is a clever metalloid that cannot decide between being shiny metal or dull rock, happily behaving like both.

q: Which of the following is a Group 1 metal that gives off a persistent yellow color when burned in a flame test, and is also used in commercial and highway vapor lamps that have a yellow glow:
e: Sodium puts on a dazzling show by glowing bright sunny yellow whenever it gets heated up in street lamps.

q: Which of the following solutions could be used to titrate an oxalic acid solution?
e: Oxalic acid needs a strong, helpful base like sodium hydroxide to neutralize it in their bubbly chemistry dance.

q: What is the difference between the two stable isotopes boron 10 and boron 11?
e: Boron-11 simply carries one extra neutron in its heart, like a twin holding a tiny little backpack.

q: When you bombard uranium-235 with a slow- moving neutron, the resulting atomic change is called:
e: That tiny neutron taps the uranium atom, splitting it neatly in two during an energetic dance called nuclear fission.

q: Which of the following is the MOST appropriate term for a mixture of two liquids that is uniformly distributed and does not separate:
e: When two liquids swirl together so perfectly that they become inseparable buddies, scientists call that happy blend a solution.

q: Which of the following pairs of types of solids and their properties is NOT correctly matched?
e: Network solids like diamonds lock their atoms so tightly together that they crack instead of bending into new shapes.

q: Given a neutral atom of iron, which of the following causes it to have a charge of +2?
e: Since electrons carry negative charges, waving goodbye to two of them leaves our iron atom feeling positively sunny with a plus-two charge!

q: Which of the following is the oxidation number of fluorine gas?
e: When identical fluorine atoms share electrons equally as a pure gas, their oxidation number is zero.

q: Which of the following substances is likely to be the most reactive in water?
e: Drop little sodium into water, and it fizzes, zips around, and throws a fiery, bubbly party in an instant!

q: The ejection of an alpha particle from a nucleus results in which of the following?
a: An increase in the atomic number by one
An increase in the mass number by four
A decrease in the atomic number by two
A decrease in the mass number by two
e: When the nucleus tosses out an alpha particle, it loses two protons, dropping its atomic number by two.

q: Which of the following is the BEST description of a colloid:
a: a homogeneous mixture of uniform particles in solution
a mixture of different substances that never settle out of solution
e: In a colloid, tiny particles stay forever floating and dancing around, completely refusing to settle to the bottom.

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of oxidation?
e: Electroplating zinc makes metal gain electrons instead of losing them, which means it is reduction rather than oxidation.

q: When four moles of solid aluminum react with three moles of oxygen gas to form aluminum oxide, this reaction is known as which of the following types of reaction?
e: Aluminum and oxygen join hands to build something brand new together, which makes this teamwork a synthesis reaction.

q: Because they contain mercury, which of the following is the BEST classification of silver dental fillings:
e: Whenever runny mercury mixes with silver to patch up a tooth, scientists call that special metal blend an amalgam.

q: The octet rule MOST directly involves which of the following:
a: only atoms with 8 or more protons
the balance of neutrons to protons
the loss of protons in radioactive decay
e: Atoms love holding hands and sharing their outer valence electrons until they reach a cozy, stable group of eight.

q: Atoms of which of these elements tend to form three covalent bonds?
e: Nitrogen loves to share, reaching out with three little atomic hands to form three cozy covalent bonds.

q: The reactivity of an element depends predominantly on its:
e: Atoms make friends using their outermost valence electrons, so this outer shell decides just how wild and reactive they are!

q: In general terms, an electric generator converts which of the following?
e: A generator catches mechanical motion, like a spinning wheel, and magically transforms all that hustle into sparkling electrical power.

q: Which of the following is NOT true for a substance:
a: pure substances always contain the same ratio of elements
water and steam are 2 different forms of the same substance
all compounds are substances and all substances are compounds
a pure substance cannot be separated by physical means
e: Pure elements like shiny gold are true substances, but they are not compounds because they have only one ingredient!

q: How do alkali metals differ from alkaline [AL-kuh- lyn] earth metals?
a: Alkali metals have one electron in their outer shells; alkaline earth metals have two
Alkali metals do not conduct electricity; alkaline earth metals do
Alkali metals are highly reactive; alkaline earth metals are not
Alkali metals are malleable [MAL-ee-uh-buhl]; alkaline earth metals are ductile
e: Alkali metals have just one lonely electron wandering on their outer shell, while alkaline earth metals proudly carry a pair of two.

q: The nucleus of the most common isotope of hydrogen is formed from which of the following?
e: At the heart of everyday hydrogen, a single brave proton sits all by itself without any neutron friends.

q: Why does the pressure exerted by a gas against a sealed container increase as the temperature increases?
a: The gas molecules move faster and strike the container wall more frequently
The gas molecules gain more entropy and hence produce more pressure
The gas molecules generate more collision energy
The increased kinetic energy increases the rate of chemical reactions between gas particles
e: When gas warms up, its tiny particles get super energetic and zoom around, bumping into the walls much more often.

q: Which of the following does NOT include a chemical reaction?
a: Immersing an iron nail in a copper sulfate solution to coat the nail with copper metal
Combining water, rocks and gravel with cement to make concrete
Combining copper and tin to make bronze
e: Melting copper and tin into bronze is just a physical mix, letting the two metals mingle without creating a new substance.

q: Which of the following phases of matter has atoms or molecules that assume the shape of their container and are NOT easily compressible?
e: Liquids love sloshing into the shape of any container, but their closely packed molecules stubbornly refuse to be squished smaller.

q: Which of the following describes a liquid in which visible particles settle?
e: In a suspension, chunky floating particles drift through the liquid until gravity gently pulls them down to the bottom.

q: At a given temperature, the velocity of gases is:
e: Heavier gas molecules move slower than tiny lightweight ones, meaning their speed is inversely linked to their mass.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about boiling liquids:
a: all boiling liquids are too hot to touch
the boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is 373.15 kelvin
the boiling point of a liquid depends on the surface pressure above the liquid
adding a handful of table salt to a quart of boiling water will change its boiling point
e: Some liquids boil at freezing temperatures, so boiling does not mean something is always scorching hot to touch!

q: Predict which object made of the following metal will sink in a pool of Mercury, which has a density 13.5 grams per cubic centimeter:
a: aluminum, which has a density of 2.6 grams per cubic centimeter
iron, which has a density of 7.9 grams per cubic centimeter
lead, which has a density of 11.34 grams per cubic centimeter
uranium, which has a density of 19.5 grams per cubic centimeter
e: Uranium is even denser than the liquid mercury, so it plunges straight to the very bottom.

q: Which of the following elements will most likely gain two electrons during a chemical reaction?
e: Oxygen already has six outer electrons, so it happily snatches two more to complete its cozy group of eight!

q: The dynamic equilibrium [ee-kwuh-LIB-ree-uhm] of a reaction is best characterized by which of the following?
a: Equal amounts of products, enzymes, and reactants
The forward rate of reaction has reached the maximum rate
The forward and reverse rates of reaction are equal
e: It is like a bustling dance where dancers swap partners forward and backward at the exact same speed, keeping everything perfectly balanced.

q: If a chimpanzee were to throw darts at a Periodic Table, he would most likely hit an element with which of the following characteristics:
e: Most elements on the board are cozy solids at room temperature, making them the easiest target to hit!

q: An inorganic binary compound always has a name that ends with what suffix?
e: Whenever two different elements team up, they love celebrating their friendship by sticking the suffix -ide right at the end!

q: Hydrogen, with its one electron, produces a line spectrum in the visible light range with:
e: As hydrogen's lone electron leaps around, it paints four distinct glowing lines of colored light for our eyes to enjoy.

q: Which of the following is NOT true regarding radioactive decay?
a: In gamma decay, no transmutation occurs
Different isotopes of the same element will decay at the same rate
Radioactive decay may cause an atom to lose protons or neutrons
Radioactive decay is a process by which unstable atoms emit ionizing particles
e: Each isotope marches to its own ticking clock, so two cousins of the same element will decay at completely different speeds!

q: In a closed system, exergonic reactions may NOT increase the available:
e: These reactions freely release heat and energy, but inside a closed space, they cannot increase the available pressure.

q: Metals A and B are both used in a circuit. Given that the temperatures of A and B are the same, and that metal A is a better conductor of heat than metal B, which of the following is necessarily true?
a: The current across A is greater than the current across B
The voltage across A is greater than the voltage across B
A has a higher resistivity than B
A has a lower resistivity than B
e: Metals that guide heat easily also let electric current glide smoothly, meaning metal A resists the flow less.

q: Which of the following most likely occurs when one molecule is oxidized:
a: there is a release in work
e: Chemistry loves teamwork, so whenever one molecule gets oxidized and gives away electrons, another molecule is reduced by catching them!

q: Which of the following elements is often added to steel to make it harder?
e: Adding shiny chromium gives steel extra strength, locking its atoms tight to make it tough and scratch-resistant.

q: Which of the following elements is NOT a metalloid [MET-ah-loid]?
e: Silicon and germanium like playing both sides, but carbon is proudly and completely a nonmetal.

q: During science lab, several students discovered that iodine dissolved readily in ethanol. In this case, the ethanol could be classified as which of the following?
e: A solvent is the liquid that welcomes another substance to dissolve inside it, just like ethanol does.

q: A fifty-fifty solution of distilled water and pure ethanol will appear:
e: Water and pure ethanol blend together seamlessly, letting light pass right through to make a completely clear liquid.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of chemical reactions:
a: energy is either absorbed or released
chemical bonds are broken and formed
e: Some reactions are a one-way trip, like baking a cake—you cannot unbake it back into eggs and flour!

q: Which of the following is largely responsible for the characteristic bad odor of a rotten egg?
e: That grumpy, nose-pinching stink comes from sneaky hydrogen sulfide gas escaping when the egg's proteins break down!

q: Which of the following metals is the best conductor of electricity?
e: Shiny silver is the ultimate champion of conductors, happily letting energetic electric sparks zoom through it faster than any other metal.

q: According to molecular orbital theory, which of the following molecules contains pi bonds?
e: Two nitrogen atoms hug tightly with a strong triple bond, which packs two special pi bonds right between them.

q: For a particular chemical reaction, delta H is negative and delta S is positive. Which of the following is true?
a: The reaction is spontaneous at any temperature
The reaction is only spontaneous when the temperature is greater than the heat of the reaction
The reaction is only spontaneous if the absolute value of delta H is greater than delta S
e: When a reaction gives off cozy warmth and creates happy chaos, nature eagerly lets it happen at any temperature!

q: Which of the following is NOT a physical property?
e: Catching fire turns a substance into something totally brand new, making flammability an exciting chemical trick rather than a physical trait!

q: A chemist is trying to pick a weak base for performing a titration. Which of the following could she choose?
e: Unlike fierce, pushy bases, potassium acetate is gentle and holds back in water, making it a delightfully weak base for experiments.

q: What type of reaction combines an acid and a base to form a salt and water?
e: When a feisty acid and a slippery base meet, they cancel each other out, neutralizing into harmless salt and water.

q: Which of the following kinds of reaction does the following equation exemplify: CH2S + 6 F2 (read as: yields) CF4 + 2 HF + SF6 + heat?
e: Greedy fluorine swoops in to steal electrons from its neighbors, making this a fiery oxidation-reduction swap meet!

q: Which of the following mixtures is made of liquids that are miscible?
e: Gasoline is a smooth team of different liquids blending together so seamlessly that they never separate into layers.

q: Which of the following is a mixture?
e: Air is a breezy party where nitrogen, oxygen, and other gases swirl together freely as a happy mixture.

q: The combination of two deuterium [doo-TEER-ee- uhm] atoms to form a single helium atom is known as which of the following?
e: Two little atoms hug so tightly that they merge into one, showing off the powerhouse magic of nuclear fusion!

q: The length of a meter was re-defined in 1983 to be based on what physical quantity?
a: The distance light travels in a specific fraction of a second in a vacuum
The length of a one-kilogram bar of iridium [ih-RID-ee-um]
A specific fraction of the length of the meridian through Paris from the North Pole to the Equator
e: Scientists timed zooming light, defining a meter by the tiny fraction of a second it takes to race across space.

q: An aspiring science student has a quantity of an unknown liquid in an unmarked, irregularly-shaped container. If a hydrometer [high-DRAW-meh-tur] reads 1.0 after being placed in the liquid, what other physical property of the liquid could be used to obtain the volume of liquid in the container?
e: Since the hydrometer gives density, weighing the liquid's mass lets you easily unlock its secret volume.

q: How many moles of carbon dioxide are required to react with 2 moles of water to form carbonic acid?
e: Carbon dioxide and water team up one-to-one, so two water molecules need two carbon dioxide friends to make acid.

q: Which of the following is the current carrier in a typical electrical conductor:
e: Electric current flows when restless little electrons wander freely through the metal, passing energy along like a merry relay team.

q: Which of the following atoms has the largest atomic radius?
e: Potassium has so many fluffy shells of electrons that it puffs out much bigger than the others!

q: Which of the following describes most of the elements on the periodic table?
e: Most elements are metals, friendly conductors that love passing warmth and electricity down the line to their neighbors.

q: A botanist observes pollen grains suspended in water jittering about in a random fashion. Another scientist observes similar random motion of coal dust on the surface of another liquid. These are commonly considered an examples of:
e: Pollen grains do a jittery dance called Brownian motion because invisible water molecules constantly bump them from every side.

q: In a closed container, if a gas is heated, which of the following occurs:
a: the gas will condense on the inner walls of the container
e: Heating trapped gas particles makes them zoom around frantically, bumping into the walls and sending the pressure soaring!

q: Copper is known for many properties, two of which in particular make it excellent for power lines. One of them is that it has a rather high electrical conductivity. The other property is that it is relatively easy to stretch it into great lengths of wire without breaking. What is the scientific name of the latter property?
e: Ductility is copper's stretchy superpower, letting it pull out into miles of skinny wire without ever snapping in two.

q: During normal chemical reactions, although the combinations of atoms that form molecules can change, the total number of atoms must remain the same. This is called:
a: the law of conservation of matter
e: Nature never misplaces its building blocks, so the law of conservation of matter ensures every atom is safely kept.

q: Which of the following intermolecular forces is strongest?
e: Hydrogen bonding acts like an extra-strong hug between molecules, pulling them together with far more power than the other forces!

q: Which of the following processes can best be used to separate a mixture of miscible liquids?
e: Distillation gently warms the liquid friends until the most eager one boils away first, easily parting the pair.

q: Imagine if you could weigh electrons and protons on a simple balance. How many electrons do you need to balance a single proton?
e: Protons are heavyweights, needing about 18 hundred featherlight electrons to balance just one on a tiny seesaw!

q: Which of the following species could most easily lose an electron?
e: Potassium holds its lone outer electron so loosely that it practically gives it away with a friendly wave.

q: For the balanced combustion reaction of methane to produce carbon dioxide and water, which of the following would NOT be expected?
e: Methane needs no catalyst helper to burn; give it a tiny spark, and it happily bursts into warm flame on its own!

q: What type of reaction is Na2S + 2HCl yields 2NaCl + H2S an example of?
e: The dancing atoms politely swap partners in pairs, making this chemistry square dance a double replacement reaction!

q: Which of the following elements has the highest first ionization energy?
e: Hugging its electrons tighter than all its neighbors, chlorine is the stingiest, needing the most energy to let go.

q: Which of the following is a halogen?
e: Fluorine belongs to a spunky chemical family called the halogens, always eager to grab one more electron to feel complete.

q: Which of the following groups of the periodic table contain nearly all of the metalloid elements?
e: Metalloids love hanging out together on a cozy staircase in groups 13 through 16, bridging metals and nonmetals.

q: Jan tosses a football to Nick by exerting a force on the ball with her arm. According to Newton's Third Law, what is the reaction force that opposes Jan's exertion?
a: Jan's arm exerts a force on her body
The football exerts a force on Jan's arm
The football exerts a force on Nick's arm when he catches it
Nick's arm exerts a force on his body when he catches it
e: Every push has an equal partner! As Jan launches the football forward, the ball gently pushes right back against her arm.

q: The electron volt is a measure of which of the following?
e: Even with "volt" in its name, it actually measures the tiny punch of energy a zooming electron carries.

q: Which of the following substances would show the Tyndall effect?
e: Blood is crowded with floating cells that bump into passing light, scattering beams so you can see the Tyndall glow.

q: Formation of a precipitate is one sign that a chemical reaction has occurred. Which of the following is most likely to precipitate in water?
e: Sulfides are shy around water, preferring to clump tightly with metals and settle to the bottom as solid flakes!

q: Which of the following real gases would behave most like an ideal gas at room temperature and pressure?
e: Tiny hydrogen molecules are so small and light that they zip around without sticking to each other at all.

q: Which of the following is formed when three atoms combine to produce a single unit of a larger substance?
e: When atoms hug tightly and stick together to build a brand-new team, they form a molecule.

q: Why are old documents preserved by sealing them in containers filled with helium?
a: Helium will react with any poisonous gas that enter the container and prevent the gas from harming the document
Helium is inexpensive and easy to find
Helium is a gas that will not react with any other element including the paper of the document
Helium will brighten the print on the document
e: Helium is a shy noble gas that refuses to react with anything, keeping fragile old papers safe from decay.

q: A C-H bond is an example of what type of bonding?
e: Carbon and hydrogen become best pals by sharing their outer electrons, hugging tight in a friendly covalent bond.

q: Which of the following is the lowest atomic number above which all elements are synthetic?
e: Nature crafted elements up through uranium at number 92, but every heavier one had to be cooked up by humans in a lab!

q: Which of the following substances contains a covalent bond?
e: Two chlorine atoms make a friendly pact by sharing their electrons like a pair of cozy mittens.

q: Which of the following does NOT depend on a chemical reaction?
a: Your voice squeaking when you breathe helium
Fizzing of an Alka-Seltzer in water
e: Helium does not change your vocal cords; sound waves just zip faster through the light gas to make you squeak.

q: Which of the following is generally NOT true:
a: the boiling point of water decreases with increased altitude on Earth
the melting point of table salt is much higher than that of glucose
metals react with nonmetals to form new metals
e: When metals team up with nonmetals, they transform into ionic salts instead of making another metal.

q: Which of the following molecules has a pyramidal [peer-uh-MIH-dul] geometry?
e: Ammonia sits like a neat little three-legged stool, where one nitrogen atom perches proudly on top like a tiny pyramid roof.

q: Which of the following is NOT true concerning pure liquid water:
a: it is a good solvent for simple sugars
it has a high specific heat
it is a requirement for all known life forms
the colder it gets the denser it gets from 100C to 0C
e: Water plays a funny trick below four degrees, fluffing outward and getting lighter instead of heavier as it freezes.

q: Vinegar is a liquid solution containing acetic acid and water. It could be accurately classified as which of the following?
e: The acid and water blend so smoothly that every single drop looks identical, making it a cozy homogeneous mixture.

q: Calcium, strontium, and barium are commonly called what kind of elements?
e: Scientists call these friendly metallic cousins alkaline earth elements because ancient thinkers found them tucked inside ordinary rocks and dirt.

q: Isotopes of the same element differ in the number of which of the following particles?
e: Think of isotopes as look-alike sibling atoms: they share the exact same protons, but carry different numbers of quiet neutrons.

q: On the periodic table, potassium is in what family?
e: Potassium belongs to the alkali metal family, a super lively group of soft metals that love to react quickly.

q: Hydrocarbons that contain at least one double bond between carbon atoms are classified as which of the following?
e: Sharing a double bond means carbons have room left over for more hydrogen friends, making the molecule unsaturated.

q: Which of the following must be TRUE for a tree that doubled its mass over a growing period of 2 years:
a: it has doubled its number of atoms
e: A tree with twice the mass gets twice as stubbornly heavy to push, which means its inertia has doubled!

q: Which of the following statements about sound is not true?
a: Sound usually travels faster in solids than liquids
The speed of sound is not dependent on the density of the medium
The speed of sound depends on the temperature of the medium
e: Sound waves actually do care about density, moving faster or slower depending on how tightly packed the particles are.

q: Francium has the lowest electronegativity of the elements. This would indicate that francium is in what corner of the periodic chart:
e: Francium relaxes way down in the lower left corner, being the gentle giant that cares the least about grabbing electrons.

q: Which of the following is closest to the potential energy in joules of a 50 pound boulder on top of a 100 foot cliff relative to the base of the cliff and given 9.8 meters per second squared as g?
e: Perched way up high, gravity gives that heavy rock about 6,800 joules of stored energy just waiting to tumble down!

q: Which of the following best describes nuclear potential energy?
a: The average total potential energy of all the protons and neutrons in an atomic nucleus
The mutual electrostatic energy of two charges
The electric potential energy divided by a charge associated with a static electric field
A force on electrically charged objects near a nucleus
e: Deep inside an atom's heart, protons and neutrons hug tight, storing up all that nuclear potential energy together.

q: The production of water from barium hydroxide and ammonium chloride is an example of what type of reaction?
e: This chilly reaction drinks in surrounding heat like a thirsty sponge, making it endothermic as it turns delightfully frosty.

q: How are ionically-bonded compounds generally named?
a: After the scientist who first created the compound
By using the name of the positive ion followed by the name of the negative ion
By using the name and Roman numeral associated with the metal involved
e: We politely name the cheerful positive ion first, followed by its negative partner, just like in table salt!

q: In Thomson's experiments with cathode ray tubes, he noted that the presence of a magnet caused the cathode rays to bend. What did he conclude from this observation?
a: Cathode rays are made of charged particles
Cathode rays are made of electrons
Cathode rays are less massive than the hydrogen atom
e: Magnets only push around things that carry an electric charge, so the bending rays proved they were full of tiny charged travelers!

q: Mendeleev [mendah-LAY-ev] organized the elements according to their reactivity. Which of the following elements would be grouped with lithium?
e: Sodium sits right under lithium in the same chemical family, happily sharing its bubbly, energetic personality.

q: Which of the following devices would need a step- up transformer to work properly in your home?
e: Old tube televisions need a huge boost of electric energy to paint glowing pictures on the screen, stepping the voltage way up!

q: Which of the following elements is NOT diatomic in its natural state?
e: While twin elements travel in pairs of two, sulfur prefers rolling around in a giant ring of eight atoms.

q: Which of the following best explains why diamond is much harder than graphite even though both are made of arranged carbon atoms?
a: Graphite is arranged in sheets, whereas diamond's layers are intertwined in a crystalline structure, making it stronger
Graphite is opaque and grey while diamond has a greater clarity and sheen to it
Diamond is arranged in sheets, whereas graphite's layers are intertwined in a crystalline stucture, making them weaker
The density of graphite is greater than that of diamond, meaning the carbon atoms are more likely to leave the structure
e: Diamond locks its carbon atoms in a super-strong three-dimensional box, while graphite just stacks slippery flat sheets that slide right off.

q: 400 joules of energy are required to boil 2 kilograms of nitrogen liquid at its boiling point. What is the heat of vaporization of nitrogen in joules per kilogram?
e: Dividing four hundred joules by two kilograms gives two hundred, the exact energy needed to boil each icy kilogram.

q: Which of the following most accurately describes the difference between graphite and diamond?
a: The carbon atoms are arranged in hexagonal planes in graphite, while they are arranged in a crystal structure in a diamond
The carbon atoms in graphite are held together by weak hydrogen bonds, while they are held together by strong covalent bonds in a diamond
The carbon atoms in graphite are mixed in with impurities, while diamond contains no impurities
The carbon atoms in graphite are bonded to more other atoms than the carbon atoms in diamond
e: Graphite stacks carbon in slippery flat sheets, while diamond locks those same atoms into a sparkling, ultra-strong crystal cage!

q: Which of the following is a Bronsted base, but not an Arrhenius [ah-REE-nee-us] base?
e: Triethylamine happily scoops up loose protons like a Bronsted base, but lacks any hydroxide to release as an Arrhenius base.

q: Which of the following elements has chemical properties similar to oxygen?
e: Sulfur lives right under oxygen in the same chemical family, so they share tricks and behave like look-alike cousins.

q: Which of the following best describes the law of multiple proportions?
a: When two pure substances react to form a compound, they do so in a definite proportion by mass
When two substances react with each other to form a compound, they do so in multiple proportions according to their mass
When one element can combine with another to form more than one compound, the mass ratios of the elements in the compounds are simple whole-number ratios of each other
There is no change in total mass during a chemical change
e: Elements team up like neat toy blocks, combining in simple whole-number ratios to build entirely different molecules.

q: If the temperature of a gaseous medium through which a sound wave passes is decreased, what will happen to the speed of the wave?
e: Chilly air makes gas molecules sluggish, so they pass sound along more slowly, decreasing the wave's speed.

q: Which of the following metals appears on flame tests as bright green and is responsible for blue colors in fireworks?
e: Copper loves showing off in fire, glowing bright green in campfire flames and dazzling the night sky with brilliant blue fireworks!

q: An element in the second column of the periodic table will have the most similar chemical reactivity to which of the following?
a: The element directly to the left
The element directly to the right
The element at the end of the row
e: Elements in the very same column are like copycat family members, sharing almost the exact same personality.

q: In 1986, the Chernobyl nuclear power plant released several radioactive isotopes into the environment. Which of the following radioactive isotopes is most likely to have replaced the calcium in the bones of people who lived near Chernobyl?
e: Strontium acts so much like its chemical cousin calcium that our bones mistakenly welcome it right in.

q: Amino acids all contain an amine group and what other group?
e: Every amino acid loves balance, carrying a friendly amine group on one side and a trusty carboxyl group on the other.

q: Which of the following explains the size of a chloride ion compared to that of a chlorine atom?
a: Chloride is smaller because it has fewer electrons
Chloride is smaller because it has more electrons
Chloride is larger because it has fewer electrons
Chloride is larger because it has more electrons
e: Gaining an extra electron makes chlorine puff out its cloud for elbow room, so the chloride ion is noticeably larger.

q: Which of the following phases of matter can change shape, but is nearly incompressable?
e: Water loves to shape-shift into any cup it visits, but its snug molecules refuse to squeeze tighter, making liquids nearly incompressible.

q: Which of the following forces is felt by an electron with charge e between two parallel plates with area A, carrying a potential difference V, separated by a distance d?
e: The electric push equals voltage divided by distance, so multiplying by the electron's charge gives eV over d.

q: Which of the following musical instruments can produce a pure tone:
e: While instruments play a rich swirl of notes, a clever synthesizer can whistle out one single, perfectly smooth sound wave.

q: The atomic weight (in amu) of an element most nearly reflects the atom's total number of which of the following?
e: Tiny electrons weigh almost nothing, so the heavy protons and neutrons huddled inside give the atom nearly all its weight.

q: John and Michael look from their 80 meter high balcony to a swimming pool with a 20 meter horizontal distance from the base of their building. If they were to jump off the balcony into the pool, how fast in meters per second would they have to jump horizontally to succeed in reaching the pool?
e: Gravity gives you a four-second fall, so leaping forward at five meters each second lands you right in the pool.

q: What term is used to describe the number density of water vapor in the air?
e: Humidity simply measures how many invisible water droplets are floating around, giving the air that cozy, damp hug.

q: A child's seesaw would be considered:
e: A seesaw is a class 1 lever because its balance point sits comfortably right in the middle between both giggling riders.

q: Chemical bonding between which of the following pairs of atoms would MOST likely be ionic:
e: Copper the metal happily gives an electron to chlorine the nonmetal, creating a strong, magnetic ionic hug.

q: The ionosphere is a region of ionized gas in the upper atmosphere. The ionosphere is extremely important to:
a: The ability of satellites to orbit earth
e: This high-flying blanket of electric air bounces radio whispers around the curve of the Earth, helping our voices travel far.

q: What is the name of the lowest energy subshell of an atom where electrons are found:
e: The cozy s subshell sits closest to the nucleus, making it the perfect low-energy spot for sleepy electrons to snuggle up first.

q: The chemical behavior of an atom is determined by its:
e: An atom's atomic number tells us its proton count, which decides how it makes friends and reacts with others.

q: Which of the following groups consists entirely of allotropes of carbon?
a: Lonsdaleite (read as: lohnz-day-LEET), graphene, and fullerene
Fullerene, lonsdaleite (read as: lohnz-day-LEET), and alamosite
e: Carbon loves dress-up, building sheets of graphene, tiny soccer balls called fullerenes, and super-tough lonsdaleite all from pure carbon atoms.

q: What impurity found in coal contributes to acid rain?
e: Sneaky sulfur hides in coal, and when it burns, it drifts into clouds to turn raindrops sour and acidic.

q: Which of the following BEST describes what atomic particle was the last to be discovered and why:
a: the electron because it has very small mass
the proton because it resides in the nucleus
the proton because it does not have any angular momentum
the neutron because it has no charge
e: Neutrons were master hide-and-seek champions because their lack of electric charge made them invisible to early detectors.

q: Which of the following laws would be most useful for determining the change in volume of a gas as it changes temperature at constant pressure?
e: Charles’s law shows how warm, happy gas puffs up bigger when heated, matching volume straight to temperature.

q: Andy is driving a car and has a reaction time of 0.5 seconds. He is driving at a constant speed of 20 meters per second when he sees a deer 50 meters in front of him. If he decelerates at a rate of 6 meters per second squared, how far away, to the nearest meter, from the deer will he stop?
e: Andy rolls ten meters before braking, then slides thirty-three more, stopping safely just seven meters away from the deer!

q: What component of the air does humidity measure?
e: On sticky summer days, humidity simply measures the invisible water vapor floating around and tickling your nose.

q: Which of the following is the pH of a substance with a hydronium concentration of 1 10-13 moles per liter?
e: Counting thirteen zeroes behind the decimal point gives this slippery, super basic solution a matching pH of thirteen.

q: Which of the following is NOT a hazard that would be listed on the Material Safety Data Sheet for concentrated sulfuric acid:
e: While sulfuric acid is a fierce liquid that can burn skin, it will not catch fire, so it is never labeled flammable.

q: Two electrons can occupy the same orbital if what value is different?
e: Two electron roommates can share the same cozy space only if their spin numbers point them twirling in opposite directions!

q: Which of the following BEST describes the following reaction: 2CaO 2Ca + O2
e: Just like a block tower tumbling apart into separate pieces, this reaction is a decomposition because one big compound splits into smaller parts.

q: Which of the following statements about precipitation is FALSE?
a: Can occur by converting a soluble substance into an insoluble form
Results in a higher purity solid if higher concentration solutions are used
Can be used to remove metal ions from aqueous solutions [AK-wee-uhs]
Can occur by changing the composition of a solvent to diminish the solubility of a substance in it
e: Crowding too many ingredients together makes them rush and trap messy dirt, so higher concentrations actually lower the purity.

q: The density of an object is a property that depends on:
a: the total volume of the object
the liquid the object is suspended in
e: Density is a secret recipe built into the material itself, so it does not depend on any of those things!

q: Which of the following is NOT an element:
e: While pure elements stand alone, sulfate is actually a cozy little team of sulfur and oxygen holding hands together.

q: Which of the following materials in pure form would register the LOWEST amount of ohms for a given electric current at 20C if all other variables are constant:
e: Shiny silver gives electricity the smoothest, easiest ride of all, offering the lowest resistance to any traveling spark.

q: Which of the following phase changes releases heat?
e: As water settles down to freeze into ice, it hugs its molecules together and gently sends its extra heat out into the room.

q: The source of the tremendous energy and rapid rotations of stars detected at the center of the Milky Way is attributed to which of the following?
e: A supermassive black hole sits at the galaxy center like a colossal cosmic drain, whipping nearby stars into a dizzy dance.

q: Which of the following materials best prevents the flow of electricity?
e: Without any mineral buddies to carry a spark, pure distilled water politely stops electricity right in its tracks.

q: A chemical reaction will always be spontaneous under which of the following conditions?
a: When it is endothermic and with a decrease in entropy
When it is exothermic and with an increase in entropy
When it is exothermic and with a decrease in entropy
When it is endothermic and with an increase in entropy
e: Nature loves sharing heat and making a messy room, so releasing energy while spreading out chaos always happens on its own.

q: Which of the following is a chemical reaction?
e: Burning lamp oil creates glowing flames that turn the oil into brand-new substances like smoke and gas.

q: The reaction of hydrocarbons found in such things as wood and paper with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide, water and heat is called:
e: Combustion is the crackling dance where fuel meets oxygen to release cozy heat, water, and puffs of carbon dioxide.

q: A permanent magnet has magnetic properties due to which of the following?
a: The magnetic fields of its electrons are balanced
Magnetic monopoles accumulate at the ends
The magnetic domains have parallel magnetizations
Its magnetic dipole moment is zero
e: Inside a permanent magnet, millions of tiny magnetic neighborhoods line up side by side, marching in the exact same direction.

q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a decaying unstable isotope?
a: It is more chaotic than random
e: Decaying atoms pop off purely at random, following peaceful odds of probability instead of wild, messy chaos.

q: On the periodic table of elements, elements in the same column have which of the following in common?
e: Elements standing in the very same column act like close siblings, sharing similar properties and friendly chemical habits.

q: Which of the following metals has the most similar valence electron configuration to silver?
e: Gold sits right below silver in the periodic family, so their outer electrons wear matching coats.

q: Under what conditions does the behavior of real gases deviate most from that predicted by the ideal gas law?
e: Squeezed tightly under high pressure and chilled by the cold, crowded gas particles stop behaving like ideal little ghosts.

q: Water ice floats because its density is less than liquid water at the same temperature. Which of the following intermolecular forces best explains this effect?
e: As water freezes, gentle hydrogen bonds push the molecules into a roomy, open pattern, helping ice float like a raft.

q: Which of the following substances when pure typically contains ONLY carbon atoms:
e: Pure graphite is like a secret club where only carbon atoms are invited to dance together in soft, slippery pencil sheets.

q: Which of the following is an electronic device that amplifies electronic signals and was used as a switching device in the first electronic computers:
e: Long before tiny chips, glowing glass vacuum tubes acted like little lightbulbs, boosting signals and flipping electric switches.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the properties of the plasma state of matter?
a: It doesn't respond to electromagnetic forces
e: Plasma is buzzing with free electrons and ions, which makes it eagerly dance whenever magnetic or electric forces tug on it.

q: Which of the following metals is often used to transform a sheet of regular glass into a mirror:
e: Shiny silver loves bouncing light so much that a thin coat on glass reflects your smiling face right back!

q: For which of the following molecules would elemental analysis give you the molecular formula?
e: Because SiO2 is already in its simplest ratio of one silicon to two oxygens, testing reveals its exact formula!

q: Which of the following molecules has the highest dipole moments?
e: Greedy fluorine tugs electrons away from hydrogen with unmatched strength, giving hydrogen fluoride the mightiest dipole moment of all.

q: Which of the following elements exists as a diatomic molecule in its lowest energy state?
e: Nitrogen atoms get lonely by themselves, so they pair up as best buddies to float peacefully through our air.

q: For two samples of mercury, one with a mass of 10 grams and the other with a mass of 20 grams, which of the following would NOT be the same?
e: Double the mercury means double the space it fills, so its volume definitely changes while its density stays identical.

q: Which of the following is closest to the distance, in meters, between the electron and proton in the neutral hydrogen atom?
e: In tiny hydrogen, the whizzing electron stays about 10^-10 meters away from its proton partner.

q: One gram of which of the following substances will be most dense at standard temperature and pressure?
e: Gold packs its heavy atoms so closely together that one tiny gram takes up the least space of all!

q: Ionic compounds are most commonly formed between what two types of elements?
e: Generous metals love giving away their electrons to eager nonmetals, locking them together in a happy ionic hug!

q: The particles in an atom that determine which element it is are the:
e: Protons are an atom's special name tag, because the exact number of these tiny pals decides which element it gets to be.

q: Acids are often defined as proton donors. Which of the following is the common form of this proton:
e: When a friendly acid gives away a proton, it is simply sharing a tiny, positively charged hydrogen ion.

q: Which of the following is a substance that does NOT conduct electricity when it is a solid but does conduct electricity when it is melted or in a molten state:
e: Sodium chloride locks its charged ions in solid crystals, but once melted, they flow freely to carry electricity.

q: Which of the following metals is attracted to a magnet?
e: Magnets simply cannot resist iron, eagerly pulling it close like a long-lost best friend for a cozy hug.

q: What is the name for the procedure which is used to separate molecules of different polarity by placing them on paper and then placing the bottom edge of the paper on in a certain polar or nonpolar solvent?
e: Chromatography lets colors race across paper, separating them as the liquid creeps along.

q: Atoms are made up of mostly empty space. Which basic force prevents the atoms of your hand, which are mainly empty space, from easily passing through the atoms in a table top, which are also mainly empty space?
e: Electrons in your hand push against the table using the electromagnetic force, stopping you like an invisible wall.

q: A balloon is filled with air at room temperature and is then dipped into liquid nitrogen. Which of the following will occur?
e: Super-chilly liquid nitrogen makes the bouncing air molecules shiver and huddle close together, so the whole balloon collapses flat.

q: Air is best described as a:
e: Air is a breezy blend where oxygen, nitrogen, and other friendly gases mingle together without chemically locking hands, making it a mixture!

q: What property of a fluid would enable a metal wire to float on the surface?
e: Water molecules hold hands so tightly at the top that they make an invisible trampoline called surface tension.

q: Which of the following best describes how a chemical change occurs in a substance?
a: It gains, loses, or shares electrons
It is ground into a powder
e: Atoms make brand-new chemical friendships by sharing, borrowing, or giving away tiny electrons to become something completely new.

q: Which of the following is a strong acid since it ionizes almost completely in water:
e: Sulfuric acid, or H2SO4, jumps into water and completely lets go of its parts, making it a famously strong acid.

q: Neon has an atomic mass of 20.19 amu. Which of the following explains why this is?
a: Each atom of neon has a mass of 20.19 amu
Neon likely has a true atomic mass of 20 amu, but mass spectrometry is not precise enough to determine its exact mass
Neon can have a variable number of protons and therefore a range of masses
Neon has three naturally abundant isotopes, but the most common is neon-20
e: Neon comes in three slightly different family sizes, with neon-20 being so popular it tilts the average weight to 20.19!

q: Which of the following is NOT a spontaneous reaction under normal atmospheric pressure:
a: rusting of a ship's hull at sea
liquid water changing to water ice at 25C
the combustion of propane in air
e: Water loves staying liquid in a warm room, so it will never freeze into ice cubes at twenty-five degrees Celsius all by itself.

q: Which of the following nitrogen-containing functional groups also contains oxygen?
e: An amide is a cozy chemical group where a nitrogen atom teams up directly with a lively oxygen atom.

q: Which of the following does NOT describe ideal fluid flow?
e: An ideal fluid glides effortlessly with zero stickiness, so it is never thick or viscous like honey.

q: Which of the following is an example of a chemical change?
e: That crispy black crust on burnt toast is brand-new stuff, and no matter what you try, you can never un-toast it!

q: Which of the following is the scientific term for a drink that settles and needs to be shaken to redistribute the particles throughout the drink:
e: In a suspension, heavy little juice bits sink to take a nap at the bottom until you shake them awake.

q: Which of the following BEST explains where the bubbles in a boiling pot of water come from:
a: hydrogen gas is produced and it rises quickly through the water
oxygen from the atmosphere enters the water
e: When water gets super hot, it vaporizes into steam bubbles that happily float right to the top!

q: For the redox reaction of tin(II) and iron(III) to produce tin(IV) and iron(II), the sum of the coefficients of the balanced reaction is:
e: One tin atom and two iron friends trade sparky electrons on each side. Counting all the teammates together adds up to six!

q: The mass spectrum for a compound has a parent peak at 80 M over Z and another peak at 65 M over Z. This indicates that what species is present in the compound?
e: A tiny piece weighing fifteen units snapped off, which is the exact calling card of a lost methyl group!

q: In order to measure the current passing through an element in the circuit, we want to connect which of the following?
a: An ammeter in parallel with the element
A voltmeter in parallel with the element
An ammeter in series with the element
A voltmeter in series with the element
e: To count the rushing electric parade, the meter must stand right in the single-file line with the circuit.

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of a physical change?
e: Rusting turns shiny iron into completely new crumbly stuff, making it a chemical adventure instead of a physical one!

q: Which of the following lists contains only metals?
e: Magnesium, manganese, and lead all belong to the shiny metal family, with not a single sneaky nonmetal among them.

q: Which of the following is NOT a naturally occurring polymer?
e: Polymers are giant repeating chains, but sweet sucrose sugar is just a tiny pair of sugar rings.

q: The addition of equal moles of which of the following to water will decrease the freezing point the most?
e: Sulfuric acid splits into three busy little pieces that crowd water so much, it gets way too tricky for ice crystals to link up.

q: When do water molecules move back and forth between the liquid and the gaseous state?
a: Only when the air is saturated
Only when the outward movement of vapor molecules produces a pressure equal to the atmospheric pressure
e: Restless little water molecules never stop dancing, jumping into the air and diving back into the puddle at all times.

q: Which of the following is closest to the diameter, in meters, of the nucleus of a zinc atom?
e: A zinc nucleus is unimaginably tiny, measuring ten to the minus fourteen meters across. It is like a speck of dust inside a giant stadium!

q: The secret to the prevention of oxidation is to provide a layer of protection between the exposed material and the air. Which of the following is NOT an example of a process used to prevent oxidation?
a: Putting lemon juice on exposed fruit
e: Anodizing does not stop oxidation because it actually uses controlled oxidation to grow a tough, colorful outer shell on aluminum.

q: Which of the following compounds is most soluble in water of 25 Celsius at 1 atmosphere of pressure?
e: Aluminum chloride loves a good swim, breaking apart and dissolving in water far easier than the others.

q: Which of the following compounds contains an ionic bond?
e: Magnesium cheerfully gives away its electrons to hungry bromine atoms, snapping them together like magnets in an ionic bond.

q: Which of the following is MOST commonly used to separate substances based on solubility differences:
e: In paper chromatography, colors race across the page, separating as the most soluble inks travel the farthest.

q: Which of the following best describes chlorine at room temperature?
e: At room temperature, chlorine drifts around as a bubbly, greenish-yellow cloud of gas that you definitely cannot miss.

q: How many atoms of magnesium are present in two molecules of the compound Mg3N2?
e: Each tiny molecule holds three magnesium buddies, so when two show up, they bring six happy atoms together.

q: Which of the following compounds is LEAST soluble in water?
e: Nitrogen molecules are shy around water, preferring to float in the air rather than dissolve into the puddle below.

q: Which of the following quantities is kept constant by a gas undergoing an isobaric [eye-soh-BARE-ik] process?
e: In an isobaric journey, a gas can expand or warm up, but its pushing pressure stays totally steady.

q: Which of the following reactions is NOT an example of oxidation-reduction?
e: The atoms here just trade dance partners without anyone stealing or sharing electrons, so no redox magic happens.

q: A chemist might use filter paper and a funnel when she wants to do which of the following separations?
