e: Filter paper catches clumsy solid pieces like a net, letting the polite liquid slip right through into the funnel.

q: Which of the following acids has the smallest dipole moment?
e: Iodine shares electrons much more evenly with hydrogen than its greedy cousins, giving hydroiodic acid the smallest dipole moment.

q: Which of the following elements has the highest boiling point?
e: Gold atoms grip each other with amazing strength, needing incredible, blazing heat before they finally let go and boil into vapor.

q: The Rutherford Experiment was actually carried out by Hans Geiger [GYE-gur] and Ernest Marsden at the request of Rutherford. Which of the following statements is NOT true about this work?
a: Rutherford inferred the gold electrons were responsible for deflecting the alpha particles by small angles
Rutherford inferred the gold nuclei were responsible for deflecting the alpha particles by large angles
The deflected alpha particles were detected as points of light on a fluorescent screen
Approximately 1 in 20,000 alpha particles was deflected by 90 degrees or more
e: Tiny electrons are far too light to bounce bulky alpha particles, so Rutherford knew they were not to blame.

q: Consider a graph with the mass of a sample on the y-axis and the sample volume on the x-axis. Which of the following substances would have the steepest slope on this graph?
e: Liquid rain packs the most weight into the tiniest space, making its density line climb the steepest of all!

q: Which of the following is NOT a property of a base?
a: Reacts with carbonates to form carbon dioxide
e: Making carbonates fizz into bubbly carbon dioxide gas is a special trick for acids, not gentle bases.

q: A student is performing an electroplating experiment in which he places two nickel electrodes in a solution of copper sulfate and connects the electrodes to a battery. He notes that the electroplating only occurs on one of the electrodes, while the other electrode remains pure nickel. Which of the following would cause the other electrode to participate in the plating instead?
a: Changing the nickel to a metal with a higher reduction potential
Changing the nickel to a metal with a lower reduction potential
Waiting until the entirety of the first electrode has been plated
Switching the terminals of the battery to which the electrodes are connected
e: Electricity only marches one way, so switching the battery terminals turns the current around and plates copper onto the other electrode instead.

q: Which of the following elements has the largest atomic weight?
e: Aluminum packs twenty-seven heavy particles in its center, easily outweighing lighter pals like neon, nitrogen, and lithium.

q: Which of the following is closest to the theoretical mechanical advantage of a screw with a mean diameter of 1 centimeter and a lead of 2 millimeters?
e: Turning around a one-centimeter circle covers about thirty-one millimeters, giving sixteen times the pushing power over a tiny two-millimeter step!

q: Which of the following is true about liquids in general?
a: Their volume shrinks when becoming a solid
They form droplets due to viscosity [vis-CAW-sih-tee]
They are more densely packed than solids
e: Most liquids cuddle up even tighter when they freeze, so their volume naturally shrinks as they turn solid.

q: Assuming equal lengths of copper wire, which of the following gauges of wire would have the greatest load?
e: Skinny wires get crowded fast, and heat makes things even wilder, giving this toasty twelve-gauge wire the biggest electrical resistance to push against.

q: Which of the following factors does NOT impact the vapor pressure of a liquid in a closed container?
a: The molecular composition of the liquid
The surface area of the liquid in contact with the gas
The intermolecular forces between the molecules in the liquid
e: Whether a puddle is wide or narrow, the trapped gas pushes back with the exact same vapor pressure.

q: Batteries require energy transfer in a redox reaction. Which of the following describes one possible type of cell in a battery?
e: Inside many batteries, a busy galvanic cell uses chemical reactions to push electrons along, powering up your favorite toys.

q: What substances, by definition, produce ions when dissolved in water?
e: Electrolytes love swimming in water, splitting into little charged ions that help electricity dance right through.

q: When making homemade ice cream, salt is added to crushed ice surrounding the cream mixture. Which of the following does NOT occur when the salt is added to the ice?
a: The freezing temperature of the cream mixture is lowered
The freezing temperature of the ice is lowered
The temperature of the system is lowered
Some of the ice is melted
e: The salt only touches the outside ice, so it cannot change the cream mixture's own freezing point at all!

q: The removal of silver tarnish by placing it in a bowl containing aluminum foil and a base is an example of which of the following types of reaction?
e: Aluminum generously passes its electrons over to the tarnished silver, making this clever swap a classic redox reaction!

q: Which of the following energy transformations occurs in your muscles when you jump into the air?
e: Your leg muscles unlock chemical energy from your food and transform it into bouncy kinetic energy to launch you skyward!

q: A friend tells you that he thinks that all processes that change a substance's color are chemical changes. Which of the following processes could you use as an example of a color change that is NOT a chemical change?
e: Adding water to dark juice just spreads the color molecules apart without changing them, making dilution a purely physical trick.

q: Which of the following liquids at room temperature and 1 atmosphere would have the GREATEST surface tension:
e: Pure water molecules hold hands so tightly that they create the strongest surface tension, acting like a tiny trampoline.

q: Which of the following elements has the highest atomic number?
e: Lawrencium wins the grand prize with a whopping 103 protons packed inside its busy heart.

q: When a hydrogen atom is in its ground state, what is TRUE about its electron?
a: It is in its lowest energy level
It has escaped from the atom
e: In its cozy ground state, this little electron snuggles down into the lowest energy level for the ultimate nap.

q: Which of the following is classified as a homogeneous [hoh-muh-JEE-nee-uhs] mixture?
e: In a solution, tiny particles blend so smoothly together that every single sip looks and tastes perfectly uniform.

q: Which of the following usually indicates a physical change?
e: Melting or freezing simply changes a substance's outfit, keeping the exact same identity underneath!

q: The plum pudding model of the atom was based on which of the following observations?
a: When alpha particles are fired at the nucleus, some bounce back
Light given off by elements in a flame test has discrete wavelengths
Alpha particles can knock positive particles from nuclei
e: Scientists discovered tiny negative particles and imagined them scattered like sweet raisins inside a puffy, positive pudding.

q: Which of the following elements has the highest melting point at standard atmospheric pressure?
e: Tungsten holds its atoms together with astonishing strength, refusing to melt even in heat that turns other metals into soup.

q: In general, metals do NOT have which of the following properties?
e: Metals are happy sharers that let electrons wander off, so they do not cling to them with high affinity.

q: Hydrogen bonding is NOT important in the physical and chemical properties of:
e: Methane particles are too shy to make sticky hydrogen bonds, so they just float freely past one another.

q: Which of the following substances has a pH value that is less than 7?
e: Tart, sour vinegar is an acid, which gives it a spunky pH score resting comfortably below seven.

q: In the radioactive decay of uranium, what is the final stable element?
e: Wandering uranium keeps tossing off radioactive pieces until it finally settles down as cozy, stable lead.

q: Which of the following atomic properties most directly determines that elements in the same group of the Periodic Table have similar chemical properties:
e: Elements in the same family have matching outer electrons, and those tiny helpers decide how they greet other chemicals.

q: Which of the following is an example of a compound?
e: Hydrogen and chlorine hold hands to build HCl, teaming up two different elements to make a brand-new compound!

q: In which of the following organizational sections of the Periodic Table are lithium, beryllium, boron and carbon all sequentially located:
e: These four elements march side-by-side in a horizontal row called a period, just like classmates standing in line.

q: The Aufbau principle is used to determine which of the following?
a: Position and momentum of an electron
e: Like sleepy campers choosing the lowest bunk beds first, electrons follow the Aufbau rule to build their neat seating chart.

q: Which of the following choices is NOT an example of a chemical change:
a: shiny new copper tarnishing to a green color
bubbles forming in a solution of vinegar following the addition of baking soda
e: Glowing red from heat is just steel blushing hot, not changing into a whole new substance!

q: Phosphorus pentachloride [penta-KLOOR-ide] gas is in a container in which it is in equilibrium with liquid phosphorous trichloride [try-KLOOR-ide] and chlorine gas. Which of the following statements would be true if the pressure inside the container were doubled by adding argon gas, holding the temperature constant?
a: The amount of chlorine gas would increase
The amount of chlorine gas would decrease
The amount of chlorine gas would remain the same
e: Argon is just a quiet bystander that ignores the other gases. Because it never joins their dance, the amount of chlorine gas stays the same!

q: Which of the following reactions is endothermic?
a: Chlorine gas reacts with hydrogen gas to form hydrogen chloride gas
Liquid water vaporizes to yield steam
Sodium metal reacts with water to yield sodium hydroxide and hydrogen gas
Liquid water freezes to yield solid ice
e: Water droplets must eagerly soak up heat from the stove before they can transform into floating puffs of steam.

q: Which of the following is the scientific term for the energy needed to transform a given quantity of a substance from a liquid to a gas at standard pressure:
e: Heat of vaporization is the exact energy needed to help liquid molecules take flight as a floating gas vapor.

q: Which of the following compounds is binary?
e: A binary compound is a simple duo made of just two ingredients, like calcium chloride holding hands with only calcium and chlorine.

q: Which of the following statements is true regarding resonance?
a: A molecule will equilibrate through its resonance structures
The nitrate ion has three valid resonance structures
Sigma bonds are most often involved in resonance
e: Nitrate shares its bonds equally among three oxygen friends, so it gets drawn in three different, equally real ways.

q: Which of the following does NOT represent a chemical reaction?
e: Falling water is just taking a splashy trip downhill without changing its identity, so no chemical magic happens there.

q: Which of the following elements has the highest first ionization [eye-on-ih-ZAY-shun] energy?
e: Oxygen clings to its electrons with fierce, tiny arms, demanding the highest ionization energy to pull one away.

q: Which of the following materials is the best thermal conductor?
e: Metals love sharing warmth, and solid aluminum quickly passes heat along like a speedy runner winning a relay race.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of pH:
a: the terms basic or alkaline describe a solution with pH greater than 7
the highest value on the pH scale is 14
strong acids dissociate almost completely in water
a pH meter operates by measuring small differences in the density of different fluids
e: A pH meter listens to tiny electric whispers in a liquid to check acidity, not how dense it is.

q: Which of the following is a diatomic molecule?
e: Diatomic means two atoms joined together, just like these two friendly hydrogen buddies holding hands in H2.

q: Which of the following isotopes was responsible for the only known naturally occurring fission reactors, the Oklo Fossil Reactors?
e: Deep underground, special uranium-235 atoms were packed just right to split apart, powering Earth's only natural nuclear reactor millions of years ago.

q: Which of the following could be used to neutralize an acid spill?
e: Calcium oxide acts as a trusty base, bravely neutralizing wild acid spills to bring everything back into safe balance.

q: Which of the following types of energy transformation occurs in a lightbulb?
e: Zipping electrical energy journeys into a bulb and magically bursts into glowing, radiant light to chase away shadows.

q: In nuclear chemistry, a mass defect exists due to:
e: Some mass mysteriously vanishes because it converts into the mighty glue, called binding energy, holding atomic centers together.

q: Which of these types of heat transfer explains how the water molecules in coffee carry scent molecules across a restaurant?
e: Rising warm air swirls like an invisible dance, using convection to carry that cozy coffee smell straight to your nose.

q: How would you turn carbon-12 into the isotope carbon-13?
e: To give carbon a tiny bit more heft without changing who it is, just sneak in one extra neutral little neutron!

q: A quantum number is not associated with an atomic electron's:
e: Quantum numbers describe an electron's energy, shape, and twirl, but its mass is already fixed and never changes.

q: The concept of "static cling," whereby electrons can be interchanged amongst materials with different degrees of electron affinity, is known as which of the following effects?
e: When socks rub against a blanket, they swap electrons through the triboelectric effect, creating delightfully clingy static hugs.

q: Which of the following best explains the benefit of adding a solution of ethylene glycol, or antifreeze, to the radiator of a car:
a: lowers the freezing point and raises the boiling point
raises the freezing point and raises the boiling point
lowers the freezing point and lowers the boiling point
raises the freezing point and lowers the boiling point
e: Antifreeze keeps engines cozy, lowering the freezing point so coolant never turns to ice and raising the boiling point against overheating.

q: Which of the following cannot be classified within the classical three states of matter?
e: Liquid crystals cannot pick a side, flowing like a liquid while staying neatly lined up like a solid!

q: A precipitation reaction is used to make which of the following?
e: Cooking sweet fudge forces sugar crystals to suddenly tumble out of the warm syrup, building a delicious solid treat!

q: Which of the following transformations is NOT a chemical change?
a: Mixing solutions of magnesium sulfate and barium nitrate
Heating calcium carbonate until it expels a gas
e: When ethanol vaporizes into gas, its molecules just float up to stretch, staying the exact same alcohol with no chemical change.

q: Which of the following is a substance that can accept a pair of electrons from another substance?
e: A Lewis acid is like a lonely puzzle piece, happily opening its arms to accept a pair of electrons.

q: Which of the following is an example of an amorphous solid?
e: Unlike neatly stacked blocks, the atoms in glass froze in a wild, scrambled jumble without forming tidy crystals.

q: If you stick a thermometer into a frozen slurry of lemonade as it is melting, you will find that the reading on the thermometer is:
a: Not changing, as long as there is ice
e: All the warmth goes into melting icy slush first, so the temperature stays perfectly still until the ice disappears.

q: Of solids, liquids, and gases,which of them can conduct thermal energy?
e: Atoms everywhere love passing the warmth along, so solids, liquids, and gases can all share thermal energy by bumping together.

q: As a solid undergoes a phase change to a liquid state, it:
a: Releases heat while remaining at a constant temperature
Absorbs heat while remaining at a constant temperature
Releases heat as the temperature increases
Absorbs heat as the temperature increases
e: The solid drinks in warmth to break free from its icy pose, keeping its temperature perfectly still until it completely melts.

q: Which of the following properties best determines the difference between a liquid and a gas?
e: Density tells the story, because cozy liquid molecules cuddle close together, while airy gas molecules wander far apart.

q: Which of the following statements best describes the properties of semiconductors?
a: They are more conductive than metals but less conductive than nonmetal insulators
Their conductivity is the same as metals
Impurities make them less conductive than metals and nonmetals
They are less conductive than metals but more conductive than insulators
e: Semiconductors are the clever middlemen, letting electricity flow better than stubborn insulators, but not quite as freely as speedy metals.

q: Which of the following compounds will be most soluble in water at 50 degrees Celsius?
e: Sugar absolutely loves warm water, happily dissolving into a sweet invisible hug much faster than the others.

q: Which of the following kinds of solutions is a mixture in which the solvent has dissolved all the solute it can at a given temperature?
e: When a drink is saturated, it is completely full of dissolved sugar and politely says, "No more sweets for me, please!"

q: Which of the following units is used to measure the diameter of protons?
e: Protons are so unimaginably tiny that scientists use the femtometer, a super microscopic measuring stick, to gauge their size.

q: For which of the following reasons is baking soda a good substance for putting out a grease fire?
a: It deprives the fire of oxygen
It removes all the components of a fire
e: When baking soda hits heat, it puffs out a blanket of gas that gently cuts off the fire's oxygen.

q: Which of the following components of a reaction is decreased when an organic catalyst is added to speed up the rate of a reaction?
e: A catalyst acts like a helpful shortcut, lowering the steep energy hill molecules have to climb to react.

q: Why do noble gases almost never form chemical bonds?
a: It is difficult for gases to form bonds
They have completely filled outer valence shells
They have very small atomic radii [RAY-dee-eye]
e: Noble gases have completely full outer shells, so they sit back happily and never need to trade electrons.

q: What makes a material a good insulator?
a: Having electrons that are bound and cannot move completely away from their nucleus [NOO-klee-uhs]
Having a nucleus that contains a number of positively charged protons
Having electrons that are farther away from the nucleus
Having electrons that can drift away
e: Good insulators are like cozy homebodies whose electrons hug their home nucleus tightly and refuse to wander off into the neighborhood.

q: Raising a bucket of chicken fat from the floor to 3 meters high off the floor would increase the bucket's:
e: Hoisting that silly bucket up high stores potential energy, giving gravity a chance to do some work if it drops!

q: Which of the following does the subscript 3 indicate in the molecular formula for calcium carbonate?
a: There are 3 oxygen atoms in one molecule of calcium carbonate
There are 3 carbon atoms in one molecule of calcium carbonate
There are 3 calcium atoms in one molecule of calcium carbonate
There are 3 atoms each of oxygen, carbon and calcium in one molecule of calcium carbonate
e: That little number three sits right beside oxygen, happily counting out three oxygen atoms tucked inside each molecule.

q: Identify which of the following factors must be measured in order to apply Archimedes' principle [ahr-kuh-MEE-deez].
a: Temperature of liquid in which an object is submerged
Density of liquid in which an object is submerged
e: To see how high an object floats, you must know the liquid’s density, revealing how heavy each splash truly is.

q: Which of the following is the most common electronic device used for storing electric energy in a process commonly called charging:
e: A capacitor acts like a tiny energy sponge, happily soaking up electric zaps when charging and holding them tight until needed.

q: Which of the following states that no two electrons can have the same four quantum numbers?
e: The Pauli exclusion principle politely insists that no two electrons can share the exact same cosmic seat number.

q: Which of the following chemical formulas best describes the following statement: "Methanol is converted to formaldehyde by reaction with oxygen?"
a: CH4O plus O2 yields CH2O plus H2O
e: Methanol is CH4O, and pairing it with oxygen gas creates formaldehyde, which is CH2O, plus water.

q: The sum of the number of protons and neutrons in an atom of an element is referred to as the element's what?
e: When protons and neutrons cuddle together in the center, adding them up gives an atom its total mass number.

q: Which of the following is the BEST description of the arrangement of the magnetic domains of an unmagnetized iron bar:
a: all are aligned at 180 to each other
all are aligned at 90 to each other
there are no magnetic domains in this case
e: Without a magnet to guide them, tiny magnetic pockets point in random directions like sleepy puppies.

q: In order for a compound to be analyzed using infrared spectroscopy, the molecule must exhibit a change in which of the following?
e: To dance with infrared light, a molecule must wiggle its electric balance, creating a shifting dipole moment.

q: Which of the following is LEAST accurate of ionic solids such as NaCl:
a: they conduct electricity when dissolved in water
e: Salt crystals cling to each other with super-strong bonds, so they actually need blistering heat to melt, not low temperatures.

q: Which of the following would be the most logical instrument to use when a small amount of suspended particles must be separated from a liquid:
e: A centrifuge acts like a super-fast merry-go-round, spinning liquid until every tiny floating speck settles to the bottom.

q: In any given row of the periodic table, which of the following families typically has the largest neutral atomic radius?
e: Starting each row, alkali metals puff up the biggest because their centers have not pulled their electrons in tight yet.

q: Which of the following properties of water is most responsible for the tempering influence of the ocean on climate?
e: The vast ocean acts like a warm sponge, using its huge heat capacity to keep nearby weather delightfully mild.

q: What subatomic particle is principally responsible for the differences in chemical properties between elements?
e: Busy little electrons dance on the outside of atoms, deciding how elements bond and play with one another.

q: Which of the following subatomic particles are charged?
e: Zooming electrons bring negative sparks while protons carry positive vibes, leaving quiet neutrons without any charge at all.

q: What is responsible for the luster, conductivity and ductility [duk-TIL-ih-tee] of metals?
a: The position on the periodic table
The number of protons in the metal
e: In metallic bonds, friendly electrons swim in a shared sea, letting metals bend, shine, and zip electricity along easily.

q: An atom's ability to react with other atoms is determined by what type of subatomic particle?
e: Busy little electrons zoom on the outside of atoms, reaching out their tiny hands to bond with neighbors!

q: An electron is emitted by an atomic nucleus in the process of:
e: During beta decay, an eager neutron transforms and zips a brand-new electron right out of the nucleus like a shooting star.

q: Water is formed when oxygen and hydrogen undergo what process?
e: Hydrogen and oxygen undergo a true chemical reaction, sparking a bond that transforms two gases into splashy liquid water.

q: A student is preparing 500 milliliters of a 6-millimolar solution of copper (II) sulfate. Which of the following pieces of glassware would be best for the most precise measurement of 500 milliliters of this solution?
e: A volumetric flask has one special line etched on its neck, making it the master of exact measurements.

q: All metals:
e: Every metal has free electrons ready to zip around, eagerly sharing heat and electricity down the line.

q: A decrease of 1 unit on the pH scale represents which of the following:
a: a 10-fold increase in the hydrogen ion concentration
a 10-fold decrease in the hydrogen ion concentration
a 100-fold increase in the hydrogen ion concentration
a 100-fold decrease in the hydrogen ion concentration
e: Each tiny step down the pH ladder makes things ten times more sour, packing in ten times more hydrogen ions!

q: Which of the following would increase the rate of rusting on a fixed quantity of iron?
a: Using iron filings instead of iron nails
Putting more water over the iron
Placing the iron in an ice bath
It is not possible to change the rate of rusting
e: Crushing iron into filings gives oxygen way more surface to touch, helping rust spread much faster!

q: Which of the following is central to the Lewis definition of acids and bases?
a: Acids donate hydrogen ions, while bases accept hydrogen ions
Acids produce hydrogen ions, while bases produce hydroxide ions
Acids donate protons, while bases accept protons
Acids accept electron pairs, while bases donate electron pairs
e: Lewis saw chemistry as an electron party where greedy acids accept electron pairs and generous bases share them.

q: At which temperature would water most likely boil on Mount McKinley:
e: High on chilly mountaintops, thinner air presses less on water, letting bubbly steam escape much sooner at ninety degrees.

q: A carboxyl group is the functional group in which of the following classes of compounds:
e: A carboxyl group loves hanging out with organic acids, giving them their spunky sour kick and defining who they truly are.

q: What phase of matter can NOT be found in a fluorescent light that is powered on?
e: Inside the solid glass tube, buzzing gas turns into glowing plasma, leaving no room for sloshy liquids.

q: A chemical change occurs when a substance:
e: When atoms trade tiny electrons, they transform from the very inside out, creating a brand-new chemical identity.

q: Although none of the following are concrete proof of a chemical change, which of the following definitely could NOT be used as an indication that a chemical change has occurred?
e: Snapping a crayon makes it smaller without changing what it is, showing that size changes are physical, not chemical!

q: Which of the following does not ultimately derive its energy to move from the sun?
a: A car with a gasoline engine
e: A nuclear submarine draws its mighty engine power from splitting deep-earth uranium atoms rather than soaking up sunshine.

q: The most useful unit of concentration in the chemistry lab is:
e: Molarity tells scientists exactly how many tiny ingredient particles are packed into every drop of liquid. It is like the ultimate lab recipe!

q: In the early 20th century, physicists were unknowingly fissioning uranium by which of the following methods:
a: exposing heavy elements to immense pressure using explosive devices in heavy-walled containment vessels
e: Scientists gently nudged uranium with tiny neutrons, not knowing they were splitting atoms right in two!

q: Atoms with one or more unpaired electrons are which of the following?
e: Lonely electrons love to dance with magnets, making these friendly atoms paramagnetic as they get gently pulled in.

q: An atom containing only a single proton and no electrons is which of the following?
e: When an atom loses its negative electron, its happy positive proton makes it a positively charged cation!

q: Which of the following compounds is LEAST soluble in water and is frequently used as a radiocontrast agent in imaging of the GI tract:
e: Barium sulfate refuses to dissolve in water, traveling safely through your tummy to show doctors bright, clear pictures inside!

q: Which of the following elements would be expected to have the most polar bond when bonded with oxygen?
e: Oxygen tugs electrons much harder than tiny hydrogen, creating an uneven, super-polar tug-of-war game between them.

q: Which of the following molecules contains the largest bond angle?
e: Carbon dioxide stretches out in a perfectly straight line, making a giant, wide-open 180-degree angle between its atoms.

q: Neutrons are approximately the mass of:
e: Inside an atom, friendly neutrons and protons weigh almost the exact same, like twin peas tucked inside a tiny pod.

q: The atomic number of molybdenum [muh-LIB-den-um] is 42. What does this number indicate?
a: Every atom has 42 total protons & neutrons in the nucleus
Every atom has a mass of 42 a.m.u.
Every atom has 42 protons in the nucleus
Every atom will form bonds that measure 42 degrees
e: Every molybdenum atom proudly wears the number forty-two, which tells us forty-two protons are cuddled inside its nucleus.

q: The carboxyl functional group is MOST associated with which of the following classes of molecules?
e: The carboxyl group has a hydrogen atom ready to hop away, which is the signature trick that makes organic acids acidic.

q: When magnesium and zinc bromide are combined, zinc and magnesium bromide are formed according to the reaction, Mg + ZnBr2 Zn + MgBr2. Which of the following types of reactions has occurred:
e: Magnesium cheerfully cuts in to steal bromide as a partner, leaving lonely zinc to dance all by itself in a single replacement!

q: Which of the following correctly explains how nails become rusty?
a: Nails attract rust particles from the air
The iron in the nail becomes another element
Iron reacts with oxygen and moisture in the air to become rust
A decrease in temperature causes rust to form
e: When iron hangs out with damp air and oxygen, they team up in a slow dance to create crumbly rust.

q: Consider a chemical reaction with a standard enthalpy change of 10 kilojoules per mole and a standard entropy change of 10 joules per mole kelvin. When is this reaction spontaneous?
e: Crank the heat above one thousand kelvins, and the messy energy finally wins, letting the reaction run wild on its own!

q: What is the mass of an electron:
a: about the same as a proton
about as much as a proton
e: Compared to a hefty proton, a tiny electron is a featherweight, weighing only about one eighteen-hundredth as much.

q: An atom of radon-222 loses an alpha particle to become a more stable atom of which of the following?
e: By tossing away two protons in an alpha particle, heavy radon changes its identity and becomes calmer polonium.

q: The electrons that are shared in chemical bonds between atoms are most accurately called:
e: Valence electrons live on an atom's very outer edge, reaching out like eager little hands to link up with their neighbors.

q: An electron in the second main energy level and the second sublevel of an atom is described by which of the following orbital designations?
e: The number two marks the second energy level, while the letter p labels its second room, neatly making the address 2p!

q: In a modern optimally functioning internal combustion engine, most of the energy is lost as:
e: Car engines work hard to zoom, but most of their fuel's energy accidentally slips away as toasty heat.

q: Alkali metals all have the same:
a: number of electrons in their outer shells
e: Every alkali metal family member shares the exact same trait: just one lone electron dancing in its outermost shell.

q: Which of the following elements has the largest electron affinity?
e: Tiny fluorine is desperately hungry for just one more electron, making it snatch them up the fastest!

q: Which of the following functional groups replaces a hydrogen in an alcohol:
e: To make an alcohol, a cheerful hydroxyl group of oxygen and hydrogen steps in to replace a lonely hydrogen.

q: Which of the following is the function of the carbon rod that runs down the center of a dry cell?
a: To keep the chemical paste moist
To conduct electrons between materials involved in the chemical reaction
To break a circuit if it overheats
e: That tall carbon rod acts like a helpful bridge, guiding tiny electrons between materials to keep the battery running smoothly.

q: When using the periodic chart, what number gives the number of protons in a given element:
e: Think of the atomic number as an element's official badge, proudly counting every single proton tucked inside its cozy heart.

q: Which of the following ions has a noble gas configuration?
e: When a nitrogen atom scoops up three extra electrons, it happily matches the complete, peaceful jacket of neon.

q: Which of the following statements is true of a reaction that has a very large equilibrium constant?
a: It requires the input of energy
e: A huge equilibrium constant means the reaction eagerly rushes forward all by itself, making it naturally spontaneous.

q: Gay-Lussac's [LOO-saks] Law would be most useful for determining temperature changes of a gas in which of the following situations?
a: Within a balloon as it is filled
e: A sturdy sealed soda can cannot change its size, perfectly trapping gas so temperature and pressure rise together.

q: Which of the following is TRUE about chemical elements:
a: fluorine is a very reactive element
rare earth metals are also known as alkaline earth metals
catalysts are typically consumed in chemical reactions
metalloids are some of the best-known conductors of heat and electricity
e: Fluorine is like an impatient puppy that desperately wants electrons, making it a wildly reactive element.

q: Which of the following does not affect the reaction rate of the Haber synthesis of ammonia?
e: Inside the sealed tank where gases make ammonia, outside humidity cannot sneak in to change how fast they mix.

q: Which of the following metals is the most reactive with water?
e: Potassium gets so super excited around water that it instantly fizzes, pops, and even bursts into bright little flames!

q: Which of the following electron configurations would be the most chemically stable?
e: With a full outer coat of eight electrons, this atom feels completely peaceful and never needs to trade or share.

q: You dip a piece of pH paper into a one-molar solution of hydrochloric acid. What color does it turn?
e: That fierce acid has so much sour power that the paper blushes a fiery red right away.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true of halogens?
a: They are nonreactive metals at room temperature
They only need one electron to fill their outer energy level
They can be used for disinfection of water and for preventing diseases of the thyroid gland
e: Halogens are not sleepy metals at all; they are lively nonmetals bursting with energy to grab new electron friends.

q: Which of the following best classifies iodine?
e: Iodine hangs out with chlorine and fluorine in the halogen family, full of colorful and eager salt-making buddies.

q: Nitrogen, sulfur, and selenium are all:
e: None of these elements shine or carry electricity like metals, which makes them proud members of the nonmetal club.

q: Elements are often classified by their atomic number. The atomic number denotes the number of:
e: Every atom wears a special badge called its atomic number, which proudly counts the positive protons sitting in its cozy center.

q: Which of the following is an intensive property?
e: Whether an ice cube is tiny or giant, it always melts at the exact same temperature, making melting point an intensive property.

q: Which of the following is TRUE of gases:
a: their particles are in uniform motion
e: Gas particles love zooming apart, leaving lots of room between them to squish closely together when you give them a gentle squeeze!

q: Which of the following is the BEST evidence that light travels as a wave:
a: a metal that is heated produces different colors
passing light through two pinholes can produce an interference pattern
light has a constant speed in a vacuum
e: Light rippling through two tiny holes overlaps like pond waves, creating striped interference patterns that prove it travels as waves.

q: Which of the following is the minimum amount of energy needed to start a chemical reaction?
e: Molecules need a little wake-up push called activation energy before they can begin their exciting chemical adventure.

q: Which of the following BEST describes a cathode ray?
a: A device that emits light through a process of optical amplification based on the stimulated emission of photons
An electrode through which electric current flows out of a polarized electrical device
A stream of electrons observed in vacuum tubes
An electrode through which electric current flows into a polarized electrical device
e: A cathode ray is just a zippy stream of tiny electrons racing happily through an empty glass tube.

q: What is the density given as specific gravity, of a one centimeter cube of a metal that weighs 5 grams:
e: Since one cubic centimeter of water weighs one gram, this five-gram metal cube is exactly five times denser.

q: Which of the following is the least dense at standard temperature and pressure:
e: Heavy metals pack their atoms tightly like crowded elevators, while gentle liquid water stays spread out and least dense.

q: Maxwell based his theory of electromagnetic waves on the hypothesis that a changing electric field gives rise to which of the following?
e: Whenever a shifting electric field ripples, it magically sparks a companion magnetic field to dance right alongside it.

q: An electrical generator converts:
e: Like a whirling wind turbine, a generator captures busy mechanical motion and turns all that spinning movement into zippy electrical energy.

q: Which of the following molecules has a tetrahedral geometry?
e: With four hydrogen buddies standing evenly around a carbon center, methane puffs into a neat little four-cornered tetrahedral shape.

q: A piece of zinc is in a beaker of water. As you add hydrochloric acid to the beaker you see small gas bubbles forming around the zinc. What is this gas?
e: The hungry acid nibbles at zinc, freeing trapped hydrogen gas to bubble up like fizzy soda pop.

q: Which of the following is NOT an acid-base conjugate pair?
e: True acid-base partners differ by only one single proton, but these two strangers are not even close family.

q: Which of the following is a metalloid?
e: Silicon is a quirky metalloid, acting half like a shiny metal and half like a shy nonmetal.

q: Which of the following elements is found in Period 2 and Group 4A of the Periodic Table:
e: If you follow the chart's map to row two and column 4A, you will discover clever carbon waiting there.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of metals?
a: They exist as extended planes of atoms
They conduct electricity but do not conduct heat
They can be combined to form alloys
e: Metals love sharing warmth, so saying they cannot conduct heat is totally wrong—just ask a hot soup spoon!

q: Which of the following has the GREATEST kinetic energy for an object moving in a straight path:
a: a mass of 2 kg with a velocity of 10 meters per second
a mass of 4 kg with a velocity of 8 meters per second
a mass of 6 kg with a velocity of 6 meters per second
a mass of 8 kg with a velocity of 4 meters per second
e: Because speed gets multiplied by itself, four kilograms zooming at eight meters per second packs the biggest energetic punch.

q: In nuclear reactors, control rods are used to absorb free neutrons without undergoing fission themselves. Which of the following is a frequently used substance to make control rods?
e: Boron acts like a calm, hungry sponge, safely catching stray neutrons in the reactor to keep things peaceful.

q: Which of the following observations would show that soil has a high pH?
a: When mixed with wet baking soda, it forms carbon dioxide
It turns red litmus paper blue
It turns blue litmus paper red
e: Soil with a high pH is a base, and like a cheerful magic trick, bases turn red litmus paper bright blue.

q: Barium will form an ionic compound in a one-to-one ratio with which of the following elements?
e: Barium gladly gives away two electrons, and sulfur eagerly takes two, making them a perfectly matched one-to-one pair.

q: Which of the following is true about a mixture of gasses?
a: The sum of the partial pressures of each gas is equal to the total pressure
The sum of the temperatures of each gas is equal to the total temperature
The total volume is equal to the largest partial volume
The total number of moles is equal to the total volume multiplied by the sum of the moles of each gas
e: Each gas gently pushes on its container, and adding up all those little pushes gives you the total pressure.

q: Which of the following is NOT a transition metal?
e: Shiny aluminum skips the middle neighborhood of transition metals, living on its own colorful side of the chart.

q: What type of bond is formed in the reaction of a Lewis acid with a Lewis base?
e: A dative bond forms because one generous atom shares both electrons like a sweet gift for its new partner.

q: Which of the following pieces of glassware would be LEAST useful for measuring a given volume of liquid?
e: A test tube is just a smooth glass cup with no measurement lines to tell you how much juice is inside.

q: Acetylene has a triple bond between its two carbons. Which of the following shapes does it have:
e: With a mighty triple bond pulling between its carbons, this little molecule stands in a perfectly straight line like an acrobat on a tightrope.

q: What type of heat transfer is demonstrated when a metal spoon placed in an operational frying pan heats up enough to burn anyone that directly touches the spoon?
e: Heat loves to share, crawling directly from the sizzling pan right up the spoon through touch!

q: Knowing that an extensive property of a system is a physical quality whose value DOES depend on the amount of the substance in a system, which of the following is an extensive property:
e: A giant bonfire holds far more heat energy than a tiny match, because heat grows with size.

q: When calculating the equilibrium constant for a reaction, the concentration of which of the following is generally included?
e: Solutes are the dissolved swimmers whose numbers can change, so chemists always count them in the reaction recipe.

q: Stars are composed of a number of elements at their birth. Which of the following elements has the HIGHEST percent composition when a star is born?
e: Baby stars begin their glowing lives mostly made of hydrogen, the simplest fuel ready to light up the galaxy!

q: When measuring liquid in a buret [byur-ET], your eyes should be at the same height as the top of the liquid for accurate measurement. This is a best practice to correct for what?
e: Looking eye-level prevents parallax, a sneaky trick of angles that makes liquid look higher or lower than it is.

q: The second electron shell in an atom can hold up to how many electrons, and contains how many different orbital shapes, respectively?
e: The second shell has two cozy room shapes, sphere and dumbbell, fitting up to eight happy electrons.

q: Which of the following is LEAST accurate regarding most solids:
a: particles in a solid vibrate around fixed positions
particles in a solid have no kinetic energy
solids have definite melting points in their pure state
e: Even frozen in place, particles in a solid are secretly dancing with a little bit of kinetic energy!

q: Which of the following substances is most likely to be able to combust?
e: Octane is the fiery champion in gasoline that happily catches fire to zoom cars down the road!

q: Which of the following would best describe a 14- karat gold bracelet?
e: Pure gold invites stronger metals to join the party, blending into a tough, shiny mixture called an alloy.

q: Which of the following electrolyte solutions would provide the best conditions for the electrolysis of water?
e: Sodium sulfate lets water split into pure gases peacefully, without greedily reacting or getting ruined in the process.

q: The organic molecule found in vinegar is an example of what class of organic molecule?
e: Vinegar gets its famous tangy splash from acetic acid, a proud member of the carboxylic acid family.

q: Which of the following will occur when an unbalanced force acts on an object:
e: When an uneven push gives an object a shove, it cannot sit still, so it accelerates into motion!

q: Which of the following solutions will conduct electricity the best?
e: Salt splits into eager little charged ions in water, building a bustling bridge for electricity to zoom across!

q: How many neutrons does fluorine-19 have?
e: Fluorine always has nine protons, so nineteen minus nine leaves ten quiet neutrons cuddled in the middle.

q: A space heater converts what forms of energy?
e: A space heater drinks electrical energy from the wall and transforms it into toasty heat to warm chilly toes.

q: Which of the following BEST explains whether a U.S. quarter will accelerate down an inclined plane faster than a silver ring of the same diameter, assuming both roll without slipping:
a: the ring accelerates faster because it has less inertia
the ring will accelerate slower because all its mass in the outer rim
the quarter will accelerate faster because it has more mass
the quarter will accelerate at the same rate as the ring since both have the same diameter
e: With all its weight pushed out to the rim, the ring is stubborn to start spinning and rolls down slower than the quarter.

q: Which of the following properties of an atomic electron is not associated with a quantum number?
e: Every electron carries the exact same unchanging mass, so nature never needs a quantum number ticket to describe how heavy it is.

q: Thermal energy spontaneously flows from which of the following?
a: A warmer region to a cooler region
A freezing material to a boiling material
e: Heat is generous, always rushing from cozy, warm spots to give chilly places a warm hug.

q: Which of the following has the highest pH?
e: Chlorine bleach sits right near the top of the basic ladder, boasting the highest pH to wash away stubborn messes.

q: Bernoulli's equation describes which of the following?
e: Bernoulli figured out the secret dance of fluids, describing how liquids swirl and how air rushes under soaring airplane wings.

q: Sodium becomes positively charged when it combines with chlorine because sodium:
e: Generous sodium happily gives away one negative little electron, leaving it with a cheerful positive charge!

q: When alkali metals such as sodium are placed in water, a gaseous substance is produced. What is this gas?
e: Sodium gets so excited in water that it kicks out atoms, sending bubbly hydrogen gas floating up into the air.

q: Which of the following is a rare earth metal?
e: Lutetium perches down in the special lanthanide row, earning its cozy spot among the rare earth metals.

q: Lanthanides are elements with which of the following orbitals partially filled?
e: Lanthanides are quiet neighbors that tuck their newest, wandering electrons right into fancy, flower-shaped f orbitals.

q: Compared to almost all other types of waves, electromagnetic waves are unique because they can travel through what?
e: Electromagnetic waves do not need anything to ride on, happily surfing right across the empty vacuum of space!

q: If 90 grams of metal has a volume of 8.7 cubic centimeters, which of the following metals is it?
a: Lead, with a specific gravity of 11.3
Silver, with a specific gravity of 10.3
Nickel, with a specific gravity of 8.9
Tin, with a specific gravity of 7.3
e: Dividing ninety grams by its size gives a density of about ten point three, pointing straight to shiny silver!

q: Which of the following best explains why clouds appear white, but liquid water is transparent?
e: Billions of tiny water droplets bounce sunlight in every direction, scattering all the colors together into one fluffy, bright white blanket.

q: What functional group can be found in acetyl-salicylic acid that is not found in salicylic acid?
e: Aspirin borrows a sweet little ester group, giving it an extra chemical cape that plain old salicylic acid simply does not wear.

q: Why does sodium becomes positively charged when it combines with chlorine?
a: It has more electrons than protons
e: Generous sodium gives away one negative electron to chlorine, leaving itself with a bright, positive charge.

q: Which of the following best describes the following reaction: 2Mg + O2 2MgO
e: When magnesium and oxygen hold hands to become one shiny team, they combine into a single partnership called a combination reaction.

q: In a nuclear reactor, moderators play a key role in helping to slow down rapidly moving neutrons. Which of the following is NOT a moderator frequently used in nuclear reactions?
e: Heavy iron atoms are too bulky to slow down speedy neutrons, making iron a terrible choice for a moderator.

q: Where are the atoms with largest atomic radii found on the periodic table?
e: Down in the lower left corner, atoms puff out their electron clouds like fluffy giants!

q: A nucleus of Lithium containing 3 protons and 4 neutrons is surrounded by 4 electrons. Which of the following best describes this?
e: With four negative electrons outnumbering three positive protons, this little atom carries an electric charge, making it an ion.

q: Which of the following has the greatest density:
e: Gold packs its heavy atoms so closely together that it squeezes way more matter into tiny spaces than the others.

q: An atom that loses its outer electron or electrons readily is which of the following?
e: Active metals are eager givers, gleefully tossing away their outer electrons to join hands with new chemical friends.

q: Which of the following loses its valence electrons the most readily?
e: Active metals are generous and excited, happily tossing away their outer electrons to anyone who asks.

q: If each of the following objects is allowed to roll down a ramp without slipping, which reaches the bottom with the greatest speed?
e: A solid sphere keeps its weight tucked neatly near its middle, helping it roll downhill faster than any other shape!

q: In which of the following compounds does hydrogen have an oxidation state that is NOT +1?
e: In sodium hydride, hydrogen grabs an electron from generous sodium, wearing a rare minus-one charge instead of its usual plus-one.

q: Sterling silver contains 92.5% silver and 7.5% copper. Which of the following substances is the solute?
e: Silver is the big host here, making the smaller amount of copper the guest known as the solute.

q: Metals that can be hammered into thin sheets are called:
e: When a metal is malleable, its atoms gently slide past each other, flattening into shiny sheets instead of snapping into pieces.

q: X-rays are composed of beams of what particles?
e: Even though they can peek through your skin, X-rays are simply high-energy light carried by tiny packets of energy called photons.

q: As you walk, which of the following forces is the most directly responsible for propelling you forward?
a: The normal force of the ground on your foot
The force of your foot pushing on the ground
The friction between your foot and the ground
The reaction force of the ground on your foot
e: Every time your shoe nudges backward, the trusty ground gives you an equal push forward to send you marching!

q: Should oxygen-17 undergo alpha decay, the resulting atom would have which of the following masses in amu?
e: Alpha decay tosses out a bundle of four tiny pieces, so oxygen-17 shrinks down to an atomic mass of thirteen.

q: Which of the following causes a drop of liquid to be rounded?
e: Water drops pull their own edges inward with surface tension, hugging tightly to form a neat little bead.

q: Which of the following molecules is considered the most polar:
e: Greedy fluorine tugs electrons away from tiny hydrogen in HF, creating a huge tug-of-war charge that makes it the most polar.

q: Which of the following is a property that is shared by both mixtures and compounds?
a: They always contain the same ratio of component atoms
They consist of atoms bound together
They retain many of the properties of their components
They can be broken down into their individual components
e: Whether atoms are glued tight or just mingled together, both mixtures and compounds can be untangled back into their separate pieces.

q: Which of the following is TRUE of a gas contained in a tall, sealed cylindrical container at 1 atmosphere of pressure and 25C:
a: the gas exerts the same pressure on all the walls of the container
the gas exerts a higher pressure on the top of the container
the gas exerts a higher pressure on the bottom of the container
the gas exerts a higher pressure on the sides of the container
e: Energetic gas particles bounce in every direction, gently bumping against every container wall with the exact same push.

q: Solvated electrons appear a vibrant blue in solution. Which of the following colors of light is being absorbed?
e: The solution swallows up warm orange light, letting only cool, dancing blue rays bounce into your eyes.

q: Which of the following molecules is an alkene [AL- keen]?
e: With two carbons sharing a special double-bond handshake, C2H4 happily belongs to the family of molecules called alkenes.

q: What is the name for the SI derived unit for energy?
e: Whenever you jump or run, scientists measure every single bounce of that lively energy in units called joules.

q: A beaker of water is placed in a vacuum chamber and the chamber evacuated. Which of the following will NOT happen?
e: Water will not heat up because rapid boiling steals its warmth away, leaving the chilly puddle to freeze instead.

q: The position of an element in the periodic table is determined by its:
e: Elements line up neatly on their colorful chart by atomic number, counting the cheerful protons tucked inside each one.

q: Which of the following BEST explains why the halogens are found in nature as compounds or ions:
a: they have an excess of neutrons and are unstable in pure form
they have 1 electron in their outer shell
they need only one electron to fill their outermost shell so they are highly reactive
they are non-metals with unfilled energy shells
e: Halogens are eager party guests who need only one last electron to complete their circle, making them react with almost anyone!

q: Which of the following substances has the highest heat of vaporization?
e: Water molecules hug each other so tightly that it takes a giant heap of heat to turn them into steam.

q: Which of the following chemical names is NOT correctly matched with its chemical formula:
e: The chemical symbol Be actually belongs to beryllium, not boron, making that name a silly case of mistaken identity.

q: Which of the following is a transition metal?
e: Iron lives right in the busy center of the periodic table, where all the colorful transition metals hang out.

q: Which of the following is NOT a base unit of measure in the metric system?
e: In the official metric club, the heavy kilogram got the badge as the true base unit, while the little gram is just a helper.

q: Molecules that have the same chemical formula but have different shapes or geometric arrangements are called:
e: Think of isomers like little Lego models built with the exact same bricks, just snapped together into totally different, wonderful shapes!

q: Ejecting electrons from the ground state of a metal atom typically requires light from which of the following regions of the electromagnetic spectrum?
e: Tightly held electrons need a giant zap of high energy to break free, and mighty X-rays pack just the right punch.

q: Given the pressure, volume, and temperature of a gas sample, the ideal gas constant allows you to determine what about that gas sample?
e: This handy math tool lets you count every single invisible gas molecule bouncing around inside the container.

q: Which of the following is NOT characteristic of an atom?
e: Tiny atoms balance positive protons and negative electrons, keeping the whole little family completely neutral rather than positively charged.

q: All liquids are:
a: Unable to accommodate the size of their containers
At a state of higher kinetic energy than any solids
e: Liquid molecules are already packed together so snugly that no matter how hard you push, they refuse to be squished any tighter.

q: When each of the following metals is added to a dilute solution of hydrochloric acid, which will react the fastest?
e: Magnesium is full of bubbly energy, eagerly tossing electrons to the acid much faster than the sleepier metals.

q: The atomic number of chlorine is 17. What does this necessarily imply about chlorine atoms?
a: They have a mass number of 34
e: An element's atomic number is its special identity card, always counting the exact number of protons tucked inside its heart.

q: In which of the following pairs are both properties colligative?
a: Freezing point depression and lowering of vapor pressure
Boiling point elevation and ionic strength
e: Both change only because of how many tiny dissolved guests are at the party, not who they actually are!

q: In the periodic table, elements are arranged by which of the following?
e: Elements line up in a neat parade by their atomic number, counting the protons tucked inside their tiny hearts.

q: You manufacture a chemical called Bowlinium that is a blue liquid at room temperature. You vigorously mix the Bowlinium with some yellow oil and clear water. Over time, two layers separate out: a green layer on top, and a clear layer on the bottom. Which of the following conclusions about this experiment is MOST correct?
a: Bowlinium is less dense than water
Bowlinium is more dense than water
Bowlinium is less dense than water and as dense as oil
Bowlinium has the same density as oil
e: Blue Bowlinium blended right into the yellow oil, floating together on top because they share the same density and are lighter than water.

q: Which of the following is LEAST accurate regarding the element helium:
a: it is the second most abundant element in the universe
it is constantly escaping from Earth's atmosphere into space
it is toxic to humans even in very low concentrations
e: Gentle helium is completely non-toxic in small puffs, happily lifting party balloons and making your voice squeak without poisoning anyone.

q: What is the term for mixtures that are not uniform throughout?
e: A heterogeneous mixture is like a wild salad where every bite is different, because its parts never fully blend together.

q: Which of the following are NOT emitted by radioactive materials?
e: While busy atoms shoot out real rays, phonons are just friendly sound vibrations rippling through solids, not radioactive escapees.

q: Which of the following is the best strategy to compensate for random errors during an experiment in an unbiased manner?
a: Using machine learning to model error
Apply a filter to reduce noise
e: Measuring many times lets random little oopsies cancel out, bringing the true answer into focus like magic!

q: Which of the following is most accurate regarding the force of gravity:
a: it is caused by the weight of an object
it is cannot travel through a vacuum
it theoretically acts over unlimited distances
it is caused by the strong nuclear force within atoms
e: Gravity stretches its invisible arms across the entire universe, gently tugging on distant stars because its reach never truly stops.

q: The smallest particle that maintains the chemical properties of a compound is called which of the following?
e: A molecule is a tiny team of atoms holding hands, keeping all their special compound powers in one tidy package.

q: Which of the following elements is NOT a gas in its standard state:
e: While other elements float off as airy gases, bromine prefers to splash around as a heavy, reddish liquid.

q: Using the International System of Units, which of the following units would be most appropriate to express force?
e: Every push and pull gets counted in newtons, named for the clever thinker who wondered why apples fall from trees.

q: During a chemical reaction, which of the following will never occur?
e: Energy loves to change costumes into heat or light, but the universe never allows a single drop of it to disappear.

q: In a circuit, electrons and electric current flow in what respective directions?
a: Negative to positive; negative to positive
Negative to positive; positive to negative
Positive to negative; positive to negative
Positive to negative; negative to positive
e: Tiny electrons march from negative to positive, while electric current was famously drawn traveling the opposite way, from positive to negative.

q: Which of the following is a heterogeneous mixture:
a: mixture of hydrogen and oxygen gases
e: Concrete is a chunky mix where bumpy rocks and sand stay separate, making it wonderfully uneven all the way through.

q: Which of these chemical compounds is NOT found in gastric acid?
e: Your tummy relies on gentle stomach salts and hydrochloric acid, wisely leaving dangerous sulfuric acid out of the recipe.

q: An organic compound is considered an alcohol if it has what functional group?
e: An alcohol gets its bubbly personality from a hydroxyl group, where oxygen and hydrogen hold hands like best friends.

q: What element on the periodic table has 92 electrons?
e: Mighty uranium is a true giant, surrounded by a swirling cloud of ninety-two busy electrons buzzing around its core.

q: How many protons are in an oxygen atom?
e: Every breath of oxygen you take is powered by atoms that hold exactly eight cheerful protons in their centers.

q: Which of the following liquids is least viscous? Assume temperature is 25°C.
e: Acetone is super runny and thin, racing and splashing along much faster than thick water or heavy mercury!

q: Which is the chemical name of H2O?
e: Dihydrogen monoxide just means two hydrogens sharing a hug with one oxygen atom, creating the splashy water we drink every day.

q: In the Scoville scale, what is the hottest chemical?
e: Resiniferatoxin is the fiery king of the spice scale, packing enough ferocious heat to make even ghost peppers tremble.

q: What was the first organic compound to be synthesized from inorganic compounds?
e: A curious scientist cooked up urea in a lab dish, proving for the first time that life-stuff can come from simple rocks and air.

q: Burning which of these metals will produce a bright white flame?
e: Magnesium burns with an eager, blindingly white glow, lighting up like a sparkler putting on its very own dazzling show.

q: Which of the following is NOT a real element?
e: Vitrainium sounds like an awesome superpower metal, but someone completely made it up, so you will never find it in the real universe.

q: Which of the following plastic is commonly used for window frames, gutters and drain pipes?
e: Tough, waterproof PVC plastic loves the outdoors, happily braving stormy rain to guard our gutters and window frames without rotting away.

q: The chemical element Lithium is named after the country of Lithuania.
e: Lithium actually got its name from the Greek word for stone, because scientists first discovered it sleeping quietly inside rocks.

q: Which of the following elements is typically used in the doping of the semiconductor silicon?
e: Sprinkling tiny boron atoms into silicon gives it the special electrical nudge it needs to power our favorite computer chips.

q: What is isobutylphenylpropanoic acid more commonly known as?
e: That giant tongue-twister name is just ibuprofen, the familiar medicine waiting patiently in the cabinet to chase away your headache.

q: In preparing to perform a flame test on a sample, a high molar solution of which of the following chemicals would be best to use to clean your nichrome wire?
e: Strong hydrochloric acid is the ultimate tidy scrubber, dissolving every leftover crumb so your wire burns clean and shows its true colors.

q: Which of the following molecules is nonpolar?
e: Four chlorine atoms pull outward equally in all directions, keeping this balanced molecule without any positive or negative side.

q: Which of the following compounds is INSOLUBLE in water?
e: While other salts love swimming, copper(I) chloride hugs itself tightly and stubbornly refuses to dissolve in water.

q: Which of the following is NOT a buffering agent?
e: Rubidium hydroxide is a bully of a strong base, so it wildly swings the balance instead of buffering it steady.

q: The unit cell in a crystal system may have one of several forms. Which of the following describes a cubic unit cell with one identical particle in the center of the cell?
e: Just like its name says, this tiny cube tucks one special atom right into the very center of its blocky body.

q: Halogenation [hal-uh-juh-NAY-shuhn] will occur fastest between methane and the radical of which of the following elements?
e: Fluorine is the most hyperactive element around, snatching methane's bonds in a lightning-fast flash of energy.

q: Soapy water is better at cleaning surfaces than plain water is because the soap changes what property of the water?
e: Soap gently relaxes water's tight skin, called surface tension, letting the water spread out flat and wash away dirt.

q: Which of the following is the final product of purine metabolism excreted in the urine?
e: When your body finishes recycling its old purine building blocks, it packs them up as uric acid to wash away in urine.

q: In which of the following ways would oxygen's electrons fill the 3 p subshells?
e: Oxygen has four outer p-electrons, so two bunch up as a pair while the other two get their own cozy rooms.

q: Assuming that none of the following molecules contain any rings, which one contains exactly one carbon-carbon or carbon-oxygen double bond?
e: With eight hydrogens for four carbons, C4H8O has just enough missing pieces to form exactly one snug double bond.

q: Under aqueous conditions, which of the following reactions would generate a precipitate?
a: Ammonium chloride mixed with potassium hydroxide
Calcium chloride mixed with potassium nitrate
Calcium carbonate mixed with hydrochloric acid
Barium chloride mixed with potassium sulfate
e: When barium meets sulfate, they lock hands so tightly they fall out of the water like solid white snowflakes.

q: Which of the following best describes the kinetics of radioactive decay?
a: It is a zeroth order process
It is a first order process
It is a second order process
It is a third order process
e: In this first-order countdown, the speed depends only on how many lonely atoms are waiting their turn to decay.

q: Fats and oils contain what functional group?
e: Fats and oils are built using cozy chemical bridges called ester groups, linking their long tails together.

q: An alkyne[AL-kine] is added to a reaction vessel containing pressurized hydrogen gas and a catalyst consisting of palladium [pah-LAID-ee-um] poisoned by traces of lead(II) ions and quinoline [KWIN-oh- lin]. Which of the following is the major product of this reaction?
e: The tired-out catalyst adds hydrogen friends to the exact same side of the chemical chain, neatly shaping a happy cis-alkene.

q: Which of the following is the molecular orbital theory prediction for the bond order of the dioxygenyl radical cation, whose chemical formula is O2+?
e: Losing one troublesome electron actually tightens their hug, giving these two oxygen atoms a stronger bond order of 2.5!

q: What color can hexa-aqua-iron (III) appear to be in aqueous solution?
e: Iron ions swimming with water molecules show off a warm, sunny yellow glow in their solution!

q: Which of the following compounds would have the largest retention factor in a TLC experiment with a silica stationary phase and hexane mobile phase?
e: Benzoic acid zooms the farthest up the paper, slipping past the silica particles to claim the highest spot.

q: Which of the following compounds is used as a fuel additive in what is commonly known as "dry-gas" by solubilizing water to reduce its contamination in gasoline:
e: Isopropyl alcohol is a friendly mixer that hugs stray water drops, dissolving them into gasoline so engines run smooth and ice-free.

q: Which of the following lattices is an example of cubic closest packing?
e: Nestling atoms tightly into corners and the middle of every square face packs them as close together as marbles in a box!

q: Who was the inventor of the first electrochemical cell?
e: Alessandro Volta cleverly stacked discs of metal to invent the very first electric battery cell.

q: Which of the following compounds is the product of the ozonolysis [oh-zohn-AW-lih-sis] of ethylene followed by a reductive workup?
e: Ozone chops the tiny ethylene molecule right in half, neatly turning both pieces into formaldehyde!

q: A system consists of two gases inside a piston. The two gases react to form a solid product. During the reaction, 150 joules of heat are released and the surroundings do 50 joules of work on the system. What is the change in internal energy in joules of the system?
e: The gas lost one hundred fifty units of heat but gained fifty from being squeezed, ending up one hundred units lower overall.

q: Which of the following is a metallic element, composes about 5% of the Earth's crust, oxidizes very easily, and when pure is a dark, silver-grey metal:
e: Iron makes up five percent of Earth's crust and loves rusting into reddish dust when it touches air.

q: Which of the following allotropes of phosphorous consists of chains of covalently-linked P4 tetrahedra?
e: Red phosphorus loves company, linking its tiny pyramid-shaped friend groups into long, playful chains.

q: Which of the following gases would deviate most from ideal gas behavior?
e: Oxygen molecules are plump and sticky compared to tiny atoms, so they bump and hug instead of flying freely.

q: According to molecular orbital theory, which of the following diatomic molecules is paramagnetic?
e: Two unpaired electrons hide inside oxygen, giving it a secret magnetic charm that pulls it toward magnets.

q: Which of the following does not describe how atoms in a CH2 group can vibrate?
e: Carbon and hydrogen love to rock, stretch, and twist together, but they never do a silly see-saw dance.

q: Which of the following is true of spontaneous processes at constant temperature, volume, and pressure?
a: Gibbs and Helmholtz free energies increase
Gibbs free energy increases; Helmholtz free energy decreases
Gibbs and Helmholtz free energies decrease
Gibbs free energy decreases; Helmholtz free energy increases
e: Nature loves rolling downhill, so spontaneous changes always cause both Gibbs and Helmholtz energies to tumble lower and lower.

q: In the notation 3d2, the 2 refers to:
a: The energy level of the electrons
The number of electrons in the orbital 3d
The number of d orbitals in the energy level 3
The total number of electrons in the n = 3 shell
e: That little number two proudly counts the two tiny electrons buzzing around together inside their cozy 3d room.

q: Which of the following compounds or ions is the best oxidizing agent?
e: Manganese dioxide is an eager little electron thief, grabbing electrons from its neighbors better than anyone else here.

q: Chlorine has a molar mass of 35.5 grams per mole. This is because chlorine has two isotopes with what ratio of abundances?
e: For every heavy chlorine-37 atom, nature sprinkles three lighter chlorine-35 twins, balancing the average weight right at thirty-five and a half.

q: The degree of unsaturation of a hydrocarbon containing two rings is equivalent to the degree of unsaturation of a hydrocarbon containing an:
e: Tying two molecular rings together locks away two pairs of hydrogens, just like the strong triple bond of an alkyne!

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven crystal lattice systems?
e: Nature loves building crystal boxes with neat tiles, but octagonal shapes leave awkward gaps and simply cannot fit together.
